dhyana.1: Om. One should meditate on her whose radiance is like the bandhūka flower, who dwells upon the seat of five skulls, whose jewelled crown bears the shining digit of the moon, and who wears a garland of heads.
dhyana.2: Her who is three-eyed, clad in red, with full, high, pot-like breasts, and who holds a book, a rosary, the boon-gesture and the gesture of fearlessness, in order,
dhyana.3: holding these, honoured by the Northern tradition (Uttarāmnāya): on her one should constantly meditate.
dhyana.4: She who is Caṇḍī, crusher of the demons Madhu, Kaiṭabha and others; she who uprooted Mahiṣa; she who crushed Dhūmrekṣaṇa, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa; she who devoured Raktabīja; the Power (Śakti) who crushed the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha; she who is the supreme giver of siddhi — may that Devī, ruler of the universe, together with her nine crore forms, protect me.
argala.viniyoga: Om. Of this mantra, the holy Argalā Stotra, Viṣṇu is the seer, anuṣṭubh is the metre, and the holy Mahālakṣmī is the deity. Its application is in recitation as a component of the Saptaśatī reading, for the pleasure of the holy Mother of the World (Jagadambā).
argala.1: Om. Be victorious, O Devī Cāmuṇḍā! Be victorious, O remover of evil beings! Be victorious, O Devī who pervade all! O Kālarātri, salutation to you. ॥1॥
argala.2: Jayantī, Maṅgalā, Kālī, Bhadrakālī, Kapālinī, Durgā, Śivā, Kṣamā, Dhātrī, Svāhā, Svadhā — you who are all these, salutation to you. ॥2॥
argala.3: O destroyer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, O giver of boons to the Creator (Brahmā), salutation to you. Give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥3॥
argala.4: O destroyer of Mahiṣāsura, O giver of happiness to devotees, salutation to you. Give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥4॥
argala.5: O Devī who slew Dhūmranetra, O giver of dharma, desire and wealth, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥5॥
argala.6: O Devī who slew Raktabīja, O destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥6॥
argala.7: O destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, O giver of welfare to the three worlds, salutation to you. Give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥7॥
argala.8: O Devī whose pair of feet is worshipped by all, O giver of all good fortune, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥8॥
argala.9: O you whose form and deeds are beyond thought, O destroyer of all enemies, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥9॥
argala.10: And to those who always bow to you with devotion, O Aparṇā, remover of sins, give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay their enemies. ॥10॥
argala.11: To those who praise you with devotion, O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of disease, give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay their enemies. ॥11॥
argala.12: O Caṇḍikā, ever victorious in battle, O destroyer of sin, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥12॥
argala.13: Give me good fortune and health; O Devī, give supreme happiness. Give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥13॥
argala.14: O Devī, bring about my welfare; bestow abundant prosperity. Give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥14॥
argala.15: Bring about the destruction of my foes; bestow strength in high measure. Give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥15॥
argala.16: O Ambikā, whose feet are rubbed by the crest-jewels of gods and demons bowing down, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥16॥
argala.17: Make me learned, renowned and prosperous. Give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥17॥
argala.18: O Devī, crusher of the pride of demons with mighty, rod-like arms, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥18॥
argala.19: O Caṇḍikā, destroyer of the pride of fierce demons, to me who bow before you give beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥19॥
argala.20: O four-armed one, praised by the four-faced Brahmā, O Supreme Sovereign, give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥20॥
argala.21: O Devī, praised by Kṛṣṇa with constant devotion, O Ambikā, always give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥21॥
argala.22: O Supreme Sovereign, praised by the Lord of the Daughter of the Himālaya (Śiva), give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥22॥
argala.23: O Supreme Sovereign, worshipped with true devotion by the husband of Indrāṇī (Indra), give me beauty, give victory, give fame, slay my enemies. ॥23॥
argala.24: O Devī, O Ambikā, you who bestow on your devotees a boundless rising of bliss, grant me beauty, grant victory, grant glory, slay my enemies. ॥24॥
argala.25: Grant me a charming wife who follows the inclinations of my mind. Grant beauty, grant victory, grant glory, slay my enemies. ॥25॥
argala.26: O you who carry beings across the ocean of worldly existence so hard to cross, O daughter of the mountain, grant me beauty, grant victory, grant glory, slay my enemies. ॥26॥
argala.27: Having recited this hymn, a person should then recite the great hymn; having duly worshipped the Devī through the Saptaśatī, he obtains a boon that is hard to win. ॥27॥
argala.iti: Thus ends the Argalā Stotra of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.
kilaka.viniyoga: Om. Of this sacred Kīlaka mantra, Śiva is the seer, anuṣṭubh is the metre, Śrī Mahāsarasvatī is the deity; its application is in japa, as a limb of the recitation of the Saptaśatī, for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā.
kilaka.1: Om. Salutation to him whose body is pure knowledge, whose divine eyes are the three Vedas, who is the means of attaining the highest good, and who bears the half-moon. ॥1॥
kilaka.2: One should understand all this — the bolt (kīlaka) even of the mantras. He too attains well-being who is constantly intent on recitation. ॥2॥
kilaka.3: For those who praise the Devī with devotion through this collection of hymns, all rites, uccāṭana and the rest, succeed. ॥3॥
kilaka.4: For him there is no need of mantra, nor of herb, nor of anything at all; even without other recitation, all uccāṭana and the like would succeed. ॥4॥
kilaka.5: “All rites will succeed” — having taken account of this doubt of the people, Hara thus placed this whole auspicious hymn under binding restriction. ॥5॥
kilaka.6: And that hymn of Caṇḍikā he made secret. One who has the requisite merit obtains that restriction and its release properly. ॥6॥
kilaka.7: He too attains well-being in full, there is no doubt — he who, with concentrated mind, on the fourteenth or the eighth day of the dark fortnight… ॥7॥
kilaka.8: …gives himself to her and receives back her grace; otherwise she is not pleased. In this form, with such a bolt, it was bolted by Mahādeva. ॥8॥
kilaka.9: He who, having made this Caṇḍī unbolted, recites it daily, surely becomes a siddha, a gaṇa, and a gandharva. ॥9॥
kilaka.10: For him there is no incapacity, nor does fear arise anywhere; he does not fall under the power of untimely death, and upon death he would attain liberation. ॥10॥
kilaka.11: Having understood this, one should begin and perform the recitation; one who does not so perform it perishes. Therefore the wise begin this in full only after having understood it. ॥11॥
kilaka.12: Whatever good fortune and the like is seen among women, all that is by her grace; therefore this auspicious hymn should be recited. ॥12॥
kilaka.13: Even when this hymn is recited softly, abundant prosperity arises, and indeed in full; therefore it should certainly be undertaken. ॥13॥
kilaka.14: By her grace come sovereignty, good fortune and health, destruction of enemies and supreme liberation; why then is she not praised by people? ॥14॥
kilaka.15: The man who constantly remembers Caṇḍikā, even in his heart, obtains his heart’s desire; the Devī would dwell ever in his heart. ॥15॥
kilaka.16: First reciting this removal of the bolt made by Mahādeva, and having thus made the text unbolted, it should be recited by those with concentrated minds. ॥16॥
kilaka.iti: Thus ends the Kīlaka Stotra of the Bhagavatī.
kavacha.viniyoga: Of this Śrī Caṇḍī Kavaca, Brahmā is the seer, Anuṣṭubh is the metre, Cāmuṇḍā is the deity, the Mothers named in the aṅganyāsa are the seed (bīja), the deities of the directional binding (digbandha) are the essence (tattva); its application is in recitation for the pleasure of Śrī Jagadambā.
kavacha.1: Om. That which is supremely secret in the world, which gives complete protection to men, and which has not been told to anyone — tell that to me, O Grandsire. ॥1॥
kavacha.2: Brahmā said: There is, O Brāhmaṇa, the most secret, holy Armour of the Devī, which benefits all beings; hear it, O great sage. ॥2॥
kavacha.3: The first is called Śailaputrī, the second Brahmacāriṇī, the third is called Candraghaṇṭā, the fourth Kūṣmāṇḍā. ॥3॥
kavacha.4: The fifth is called Skandamātā, the sixth likewise Kātyāyanī, the seventh Kālarātri, and the eighth is called Mahāgaurī. ॥4॥
kavacha.5: And the ninth is Siddhidātrī; thus the nine Durgās are proclaimed. These names were spoken by the great-souled Brahmā himself. ॥5॥
kavacha.6: Those who are being burnt by fire, who have fallen among enemies in battle, who are in difficult and impassable places, stricken with fear — if they have taken refuge in the Devī, ॥6॥
kavacha.7: no misfortune whatever arises for them in the peril of battle, nor do they see calamity that brings grief, sorrow and fear. ॥7॥
kavacha.8: Those by whom you are remembered constantly with devotion, for them prosperity arises. Those who remember you, O Queen of the gods, you protect them — there is no doubt. ॥8॥
kavacha.9: Cāmuṇḍā is seated on a corpse, Vārāhī rides a buffalo, Aindrī is mounted on an elephant, Vaiṣṇavī is seated on Garuḍa. ॥9॥
kavacha.10: Nārasiṃhī is of great valour, Śivadūtī of great strength, Māheśvarī rides a bull, Kaumārī has the peacock as her mount. ॥10॥
kavacha.11: The goddess Lakṣmī is seated on a lotus, holds a lotus in her hand, and is beloved of Hari; the goddess Īśvarī bears a white form and has a bull as her mount. ॥11॥
kavacha.12: Brāhmī is mounted on a swan, adorned with all ornaments. Thus all these Mothers are endowed with every yogic power. ॥12॥
kavacha.13: All of them are rich in the splendour of various ornaments, beautified with various gems, and with excellent pearls in divine necklaces hanging down, ॥13॥
kavacha.14: with sapphires, great blue gems and splendid rubies — the goddesses are seen mounted on chariots, filled with wrath. ॥14॥
kavacha.15: Conch, discus, mace, spear, plough and the pestle weapon, shield, javelin, axe and noose, ॥15॥
kavacha.16: the lance, the trident and the excellent weapon Śārṅga bow — for destroying the bodies of the Daityas and for granting fearlessness to devotees, ॥16॥
kavacha.17: they bear weapons thus, and indeed for the welfare of the gods. Salutation be to you, O greatly fierce one, O you of greatly terrible valour! ॥17॥
kavacha.18: O you of great strength, of great energy, destroyer of great fears, protect me, O Devī, hard to behold, who increase the fear of enemies! ॥18॥
kavacha.19: May Aindrī protect me in the east, the Fire-deity in the south-east; may Vārāhī guard me in the south, the Sword-bearer in the south-west. ॥19॥
kavacha.20: May Vāruṇī protect me in the west, the one riding a deer in the north-west; may Kauberī guard in the north, the trident-bearer in the north-east. ॥20॥
kavacha.21: May Brahmāṇī protect me above, and Vaiṣṇavī likewise below; thus may Cāmuṇḍā, whose mount is a corpse, protect the ten directions. ॥21॥
kavacha.22: May Jayā guard me in front, may Vijayā guard me behind, Ajitā on the left side, and Aparājitā on the right. ॥22॥
kavacha.23: May Dyotinī protect my topknot, Umā stationed on the crown of the head, Mālādharī on the forehead, and may Yaśasvinī protect the eyebrows. ॥23॥
kavacha.24: May Citranetrā protect the eyes, and Yamaghaṇṭā the sides; Trinetrā protect me with her trident, and Caṇḍikā the place between the eyebrows. ॥24॥
kavacha.25: May Śaṅkhinī protect the space between the eyes, Dvāravāsinī the ears; may Kālikā protect the cheeks, and Śaṅkarī the roots of the ears. ॥25॥
kavacha.26: May Sugandhā protect the nose, and Carcikā the upper lip; Amṛtābālā the lower lip, and Sarasvatī the tongue. ॥26॥
kavacha.27: May Kaumārī protect the teeth, and Caṇḍikā the region of the throat; Citraghaṇṭā the uvula, and Mahāmāyā the palate. ॥27॥
kavacha.28: May Kāmākṣī protect the chin, and Sarvamaṅgalā my speech; Bhadrakālī the neck, and Dhanurdharī the spine. ॥28॥
kavacha.29: May Nīlagrīvā protect the outer throat, Nalakūbarī the windpipe; may Khaḍginī protect the shoulders, and Vajradhāriṇī my arms. ॥29॥
kavacha.30: May Daṇḍinī protect the hands, and Ambikā the fingers; may Śūleśvarī protect the nails, and Nareśvarī protect the belly. ॥30॥
kavacha.31: May Mahādevī, destroyer of the mind’s sorrow, protect the breasts; Devī Lalitā the heart, and Śūladhāriṇī the abdomen. ॥31॥
kavacha.32: May Kāminī protect the navel, and likewise Guhyeśvarī the private parts; may Durgandhā protect the generative organ, and Guhyavāhinī my anus. ॥32॥
kavacha.33: May Bhagavatī protect the waist, and Meghavāhanā my thighs; may Mahābalā protect the shanks, and Mādhavanāyikā the knees. ॥33॥
kavacha.34: May Nārasiṃhī protect the ankles, and Kauśikī the tops of the feet; Śrīdharī the toes, and Pātālavāsinī the soles. ॥34॥
kavacha.35: May Daṃṣṭrakarālī protect the nails, and Ūrdhvakeśinī the hair; Kaumārī the pores of the skin, and likewise Yogīśvarī the skin. ॥35॥
kavacha.36: May Pārvatī protect the blood, marrow, fat, flesh, bones and fatty tissue; Kālarātri the intestines, and Mukuṭeśvarī the bile. ॥36॥
kavacha.37: May Padmāvatī protect the lotus-sheath of the heart, and likewise Cūḍāmaṇi the phlegm; Jvālāmukhī the lustre of the nails, and Abhedyā all the joints. ॥37॥
kavacha.38: May Brahmāṇī protect my semen, and likewise Chatreśvarī my shadow; may Dharmadhāriṇī protect my ego, mind and intellect. ॥38॥
kavacha.39: May Vajrahastā protect my prāṇa and apāna, as also vyāna, udāna and samāna; and may Kalyāṇaśobhanā protect my life-breaths. ॥39॥
kavacha.40: May Yoginī protect me in taste, form, smell, sound and touch; may Nārāyaṇī always protect sattva, rajas and tamas. ॥40॥
kavacha.41: May Vārāhī protect my life-span, may Pārvatī protect my dharma; may Vaiṣṇavī always protect my glory, fame and prosperity. ॥41॥
kavacha.42: May Indrāṇī protect my lineage, and may Caṇḍikā protect my cattle; may Mahālakṣmī protect my sons, and may Bhairavī protect my wife. ॥42॥
kavacha.43: May Dhaneśvarī protect my wealth, and likewise Kaumārī my daughter; may Supathā protect the path, and likewise Kṣemaṅkarī the road. ॥43॥
kavacha.44: May Mahālakṣmī protect me at the king’s gate, and Vijayā, ever abiding everywhere. And whatever place is without protection, left uncovered by the kavaca — ॥44॥
kavacha.45: — all that protect for me, O Devī, Jayantī, destroyer of sin. One should always recite this holy kavaca, which gives protection in every way. ॥45॥
kavacha.46: O brahmin sage, this secret has been told by me to you out of devotion. If one desires one’s own welfare, one should not go even a single step without the kavaca. ॥46॥
kavacha.47: Whoever, always covered by the kavaca, goes wherever he goes — there and there he finds gain of wealth and victory at all times. ॥47॥
kavacha.48: Whatever desire he thinks of, that he surely obtains; such a man will attain supreme, unequalled sovereignty on earth. ॥48॥
kavacha.49: A mortal becomes fearless and unconquered in battles. A man covered by the Kavaca becomes worthy of worship in the three worlds. ॥49॥
kavacha.50: This Kavaca of the Devī is hard to obtain even for the gods. Whoever, self-controlled and endowed with faith, recites it daily at the three junctions of the day — ॥50॥
kavacha.51: — divine power comes to him, and he is unconquered in the three worlds. He lives a hundred years and more, free from untimely death. ॥51॥
kavacha.52: All diseases perish, such as spider-poison sores, boils and the like; and whatever poison there is — from immobile things, from moving creatures, or artificially prepared — also perishes. ॥52॥
kavacha.53: All hostile rites, the mantras and yantras used against one on earth; beings moving on earth and moving in the sky, those arising in the family and those acquired through instruction — ॥53॥
kavacha.54: afflictions innate and hereditary, Mālā, Ḍākinī and Śākinī too, the terrible Ḍākinīs moving in the mid-air, of mighty roar — ॥54॥
kavacha.55: Grahas, Bhūtas and Piśācas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas, Brahmarākṣasas and Vetālas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, Bhairavas and the like — ॥55॥
kavacha.56: — all these perish at the mere sight of him who is covered by the Kavaca. Rise in honour comes to him from the king, and his splendour increases supremely. ॥56॥
kavacha.57: Increase of renown comes to men, and increase of fame arises. Therefore, O sage, a devotee should always recite the Kavaca, which grants desires. ॥57॥
kavacha.58: Having first recited the Kavaca, one should recite the Caṇḍī Saptaśatī. Then the accomplishment born of reciting the Caṇḍī comes about without obstacle. ॥58॥
kavacha.59: As long as the sphere of the earth endures, with its mountains, woods and forests, so long do his sons and grandsons, his lineage, remain upon the earth. ॥59॥
kavacha.60: At the end of the body, by the grace of Mahāmāyā, the man attains the supreme, eternal abode, very hard to reach even for the gods. ॥60॥
kavacha.61: He goes there, and having gone, there is no coming back again. He gains the supreme abode and attains equality with Śiva. ॥61॥
kavacha.iti: Thus ends the Devī Kavaca of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, composed by Hari, Hara and Brahmā.
1.viniyoga: Of this sacred First Episode (prathama caritra): Brahmā is the seer; Mahākālī is the deity; Gāyatrī is the metre; Nandā is the power (śakti); Raktadantikā is the seed (bīja); fire is the principle (tattva); the Ṛgveda is its essential form. Its application is in the recitation of the First Episode, for the pleasure of Śrī Mahākālī.
1.dhyana: Om. I worship Mahākālikā, who holds in her hands sword, discus, mace, arrows, bow, iron club, trident, bhuśuṇḍī, a severed head and a conch; who is three-eyed, covered with ornaments on all her limbs, with the lustre of a blue gem, having ten faces and ten feet; whom the lotus-born Brahmā praised, when Hari was asleep, in order to slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
1.2: Sāvarṇi, the son of the Sun, who is called the eighth Manu — hear of his origin from me as I tell it in detail. ॥2॥
1.3: Hear how, by the power of Mahāmāyā, that illustrious Sāvarṇi, son of Ravi (the Sun), became the lord of a Manvantara. ॥3॥
1.4: Formerly, in the Svārociṣa Manvantara, there was a king named Suratha, born of the Caitra dynasty, ruling over the whole circle of the earth. ॥4॥
1.5: While he was properly protecting his subjects as if they were his own sons, kings who were Kolāvidhvaṃsins (destroyers of Kolā) then became his enemies. ॥5॥
1.6: There was a war between him, who wielded a very mighty rod of power, and them; and in battle he was defeated by those Kolāvidhvaṃsins, even though they were fewer. ॥6॥
1.7: Then, having come back to his own city, he became ruler of his own country alone. Then that illustrious one was attacked by those powerful enemies. ॥7॥
1.8: Then, even there in his own city, his treasury and army were seized from him, now weakened, by his powerful, wicked and evil-minded ministers. ॥8॥
1.9: Then, under the pretext of hunting, that king, deprived of his sovereignty, mounted a horse alone and went into a dense forest. ॥9॥
1.10: There he saw the hermitage of Medhas, the best of the twice-born, filled with wild beasts grown peaceful and graced by the sage’s disciples. ॥10॥
1.11: And, honoured by that sage, he stayed for some time, wandering here and there in that hermitage of the excellent sage. ॥11॥
1.12: Then, there, his mind drawn by possessiveness, he thought: ‘That city, formerly protected by my forefathers, is now indeed bereft of me.’ ॥12॥
1.13: ‘Whether it is being protected righteously or not by those servants of mine of evil conduct, I do not know. That chief elephant of mine, heroic and always in rut —’ ॥13॥
1.14: ‘— having fallen into the power of my enemies, what enjoyments will he get? Those who always followed me, receiving favours, wealth and food —’ ॥14॥
1.15: ‘— surely they today pay court to other kings. By those given to improper spending, who constantly make expenditure —’ ॥15॥
1.16: ‘— the treasury that I accumulated with great hardship will go to ruin.’ This and other things the king kept pondering constantly. ॥16॥
1.17: There, near the brahmin’s hermitage, he saw a merchant. He was asked by him: Who are you, sir? And what is the reason for your coming here? ॥17॥
1.18: ‘Why do you appear as if grief-stricken, as if dejected?’ Having heard these words of the king, spoken with affection — ॥18॥
1.19: — that merchant, bowing with humility, replied to the king. ॥19॥
1.21: I am a merchant named Samādhi, born in a family of wealthy people. ॥21॥
1.22: And I have been driven out by my wicked sons and wife out of greed for wealth; and, they having taken my wealth, I am bereft of wealth, wife and sons. ॥22॥
1.23: Grieving, cast out by my trusted kinsmen, I have come to the forest. Such as I am, I do not know the news, whether of welfare or of ill, of my sons… ॥23॥
1.24: … nor the news of my kinsmen and of my wife, while I remain here. Is there now welfare in their home, or is there misfortune? ॥24॥
1.25: How are they? Are my sons of good conduct, or are they of bad conduct? ॥25॥
1.27: Those greedy ones—sons, wife and the rest—by whom you were driven out on account of wealth, ॥27॥
1.28: why does your mind bind itself in affection to them? ॥28॥
1.30: It is just as you have said—these words concerning me. ॥30॥
1.31: What can I do? My mind does not take on harshness towards those who, greedy for wealth, abandoning love for their father, have cast me out, ॥31॥
1.32: and abandoning affection for husband and kin—yet my mind is full of affection for them alone. What is this? I do not understand it, though I know, O wise one. ॥32॥
1.33: that my mind is inclined to love even towards worthless kinsmen. For their sake sighing and dejection arise in me. ॥33॥
1.34: What can I do, since my mind does not become hard towards those unloving ones? ॥34॥
1.36: Then, O Brāhmaṇa, the two together approached that sage. ॥36॥
1.37: That vaiśya named Samādhi and that best of kings, having exchanged greetings with him as was proper and fitting, ॥37॥
1.38: sat down, and the vaiśya and the king held some conversation. ॥38॥
1.40: O revered one, I wish to ask you one thing; please tell me that. ॥40॥
1.41: That, to the distress of my mind, which lacks control over itself, there is in me—who have lost my kingdom—attachment to all the limbs of the kingdom, ॥41॥
1.42: even though I know, as if I were ignorant—what is this, O best of sages? And this man has been humiliated by his sons, wife and servants, and abandoned, ॥42॥
1.43: and forsaken by his kin; yet he is exceedingly affectionate towards them. Thus he and I are both deeply distressed. ॥43॥
1.44: our minds drawn by attachment to objects whose faults we have seen. So what is this, O fortunate one, that delusion besets even us two who have knowledge? ॥44॥
1.45: This bewilderment arises in me and in him, blind in discrimination. ॥45॥
1.47: Every creature has knowledge within the range of sense-objects. ॥47॥
1.48: And sense-objects, O greatly fortunate one, thus come to beings each in its own separate way. Some creatures are blind by day, and others likewise are blind at night. ॥48॥
1.49: Some creatures have equal sight by day and by night. Humans are indeed possessed of knowledge, but they are certainly not the only ones. ॥49॥
1.50: For all cattle, birds, wild beasts and the like are possessed of knowledge; and the knowledge humans have is the same as that of those beasts and birds. ॥50॥
1.51: And what humans have, they the animals have too, and the rest is likewise common to both. Even though knowledge is present, look at these birds placing grain into the beaks of their young, ॥51॥
1.52: intent on dropping grains into them out of delusion, even while tormented by hunger themselves. Humans, O tiger among men, are full of longing towards their sons, ॥52॥
1.53: out of greed, expecting a return of the favour; do you not see them? Even so, they are cast into the pit of delusion with its whirlpool of possessiveness, ॥53॥
1.54: by the power of Mahāmāyā, who sustains the continuance of worldly existence. Therefore one should feel no wonder at this: she is the Yoganidrā of the Lord of the world. ॥54॥
1.55: She is the Mahāmāyā of Hari; by her the world is deluded. For she, the Devī Bhagavatī, seizes the minds even of the wise, ॥55॥
1.56: having forcibly drawn them away, Mahāmāyā delivers them to delusion. By her this entire universe, moving and unmoving, is created. ॥56॥
1.57: When she is pleased, she becomes the giver of boons to men for their liberation. She is the supreme knowledge, the cause of liberation, eternal; ॥57॥
1.58: and she alone is the cause of bondage to worldly existence; she is the sovereign over all lords. ॥58॥
1.60: O revered one, who indeed is that goddess whom you call Mahāmāyā? ॥60॥
1.61: whom you speak of? How did she arise, and what is her work, O twice-born? Of what power is that Devī, of what nature, and of what origin? ॥61॥
1.62: All that I wish to hear from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman. ॥62॥
1.64: She is eternal indeed, having the world as her form; by her all this is pervaded. ॥64॥
1.65: Even so, hear from me of her manifestation in many ways. When she appears to accomplish the purpose of the gods, ॥65॥
1.66: then, though eternal, she is said in the world to have been born. When Viṣṇu, the world having become a single ocean, ॥66॥
1.67: having spread out Śeṣa as his bed, the blessed Lord resorted to yogic sleep at the end of the kalpa, then two terrible asuras, the renowned Madhu and Kaiṭabha, ॥67॥
1.68: sprung from the wax of Viṣṇu’s ears, rose up to slay Brahmā. That Brahmā, the lord of creatures, seated in the lotus of Viṣṇu’s navel, ॥68॥
1.69: seeing those two fierce asuras and Janārdana fast asleep, remaining with single-pointed heart, praised that Yoganidrā, ॥69॥
1.70: in order to awaken Hari — her who had made her abode in Hari’s eyes, the sovereign of the universe, the sustainer of the world, the cause of its maintenance and dissolution, ॥70॥
1.71: the lord of radiance Brahmā praised Bhagavatī Nidrā, the incomparable Sleep of Viṣṇu. ॥71॥
1.73: You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, you indeed are the Vaṣaṭ-call; your very self is the sacred sound (svara). ॥73॥
1.74: You are the nectar of immortality; in the eternal imperishable syllable Om you abide threefold as its measures; and you are the eternal half-measure, which cannot be uttered distinctly. ॥74॥
1.75: You alone are Sandhyā and Sāvitrī; you, O Devī, are the supreme mother. By you this universe is upheld; by you this world is created. ॥75॥
1.76: By you it is protected, O Devī, and you always consume it at the end. At its emanation you are the form of creation, and in protecting it the form of preservation; ॥76॥
1.77: so too, at the end of this world, you are the form of dissolution, O you who pervade the world. You are the great knowledge, the great illusion (Mahāmāyā), the great intellect, the great memory, ॥77॥
1.78: and you are the great delusion, the great Devī, the great sovereign. You are the primal nature (Prakṛti) of all, bringing forth the three guṇas. ॥78॥
1.79: You are the Night of Time, the Great Night, and the dreadful Night of Delusion. You are Śrī, you are the sovereign, you are modesty (Hrī), you are understanding, marked by awareness; ॥79॥
1.80: shame, nourishment and contentment; you are peace and forbearance too. Terrible, you bear the sword, the trident, the mace and the discus, ॥80॥
1.81: the conch and the bow, with arrows, bhuśuṇḍī and iron club as your weapons. You are gentle, gentler still, and indeed far more beautiful than all gentle things. ॥81॥
1.82: You alone are the highest of the high and the low, the supreme sovereign. And whatever thing exists anywhere, real or unreal, O Self of all, ॥82॥
1.83: the power of all that is you; how can you be praised by me? By you, by whom even he who creates the world, protects the world and devours the world ॥83॥
1.84: even he has been brought under the sway of sleep; who here is able to praise you? Viṣṇu, I, and Īśāna Śiva too ॥84॥
1.85: have been made by you to take on bodies; therefore who could be capable of praising you? O Devī, thus praised as you are for your own exalted powers, ॥85॥
1.86: delude these two invincible asuras, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and let Acyuta, lord of the world, be quickly brought to wakefulness, ॥86॥
1.87: and let awareness be roused in him, so that he may slay these two great asuras. ॥87॥
1.89: Thus praised there and then by Brahmā (Vedhas), the Devī of tamas, ॥89॥
1.90: in order to awaken Viṣṇu and to slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, from his eyes, mouth, nose, arms and heart, and likewise from his chest, ॥90॥
1.91: emerged and stood in the sight of Brahmā, whose birth is from the Unmanifest. And released by her, Janārdana, lord of the world, arose. ॥91॥
1.92: from his serpent-bed on the single ocean; then he saw those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, evil-minded, of exceeding strength and valour, ॥92॥
1.93: their eyes red with anger, set on devouring Brahmā. Then, rising up, the Lord Hari fought with them ॥93॥
1.94: for five thousand years, the all-pervading one using his arms as weapons. And those two, maddened by their excessive strength and deluded by Mahāmāyā, ॥94॥
1.95: said to Keśava, ‘Choose a boon from us.’ ॥95॥
1.97: If you two are pleased with me, then today may both of you be slain by me. ॥97॥
1.98: What need is there of any other boon here? For this much alone has been chosen by me. ॥98॥
1.100: Thus deceived, the two demons then saw that the whole world was made of water. ॥100॥
1.101: Having looked at it, the lotus-eyed Lord was addressed by the two: Slay us where the earth is not flooded with water. ॥101॥
1.103: Saying “So be it,” the Lord who bears the conch, discus and mace placed them on his thigh, and their two heads were severed by his discus. ॥103॥
1.104: Thus did she herself arise, praised by Brahmā. Now hear further the power of this Devī; I shall tell you. ॥104॥
1.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the first adhyāya, named the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha. ॥1॥
2.viniyoga: Of this sacred Middle Episode (Madhyama Caritra), Viṣṇu is the seer, Śrī Mahālakṣmī is the deity, Uṣṇik is the metre, Śākambharī is the power (śakti), Durgā is the seed (bīja), Air is the element (tattva), and the Yajurveda is its essential form. Its application is in the recitation of the Middle Episode for the pleasure of Śrī Mahālakṣmī.
2.dhyana: Om. I worship here Mahālakṣmī, crusher of the buffalo demon, seated on a lotus, with the lustre of coral, who holds in her hands a rosary and an axe, a mace, an arrow and a thunderbolt, a lotus, a bow, a water-pot, a staff, a spear, a sword and a shield, a conch, a bell, a wine-cup, a trident, a noose and the Sudarśana discus.
2.1: Om hrīṃ. The sage Medhas said: ॥1॥
2.2: Long ago there was a war between the gods and the asuras for a full hundred years, when Mahiṣa was the lord of the asuras and Purandara (Indra) the lord of the gods. ॥2॥
2.3: There the army of the gods was defeated by the mighty asuras, and having conquered all the gods, Mahiṣāsura became Indra. ॥3॥
2.4: Then the defeated gods, placing at their head Brahmā, the lotus-born lord of creatures, went to where Īśa (Śiva) and the one with the Garuḍa banner (Viṣṇu) were. ॥4॥
2.5: The gods related to those two exactly as it had happened the deeds of Mahiṣāsura and the full account of the gods defeat. ॥5॥
2.6: He himself has taken over the offices of Sūrya, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, Candra, Yama and Varuṇa, and of the others too. ॥6॥
2.7: Driven out of heaven by that wicked Mahiṣa, all the hosts of gods wander on earth like mortals. ॥7॥
2.8: We have told you all this, the doings of the enemy of the immortals. We have come to you for refuge; let his slaying be thought out. ॥8॥
2.9: Hearing these words of the gods, Madhusūdana (Viṣṇu) and Śambhu (Śiva) became angry, their faces twisted with frowning brows. ॥9॥
2.10: Then from the face of the Discus-bearer (Viṣṇu), filled with great wrath, there came forth a mighty radiance, and likewise from Brahmā and from Śaṅkara. ॥10॥
2.11: And from the bodies of the other gods too, Śakra (Indra) and the rest, a very great radiance came forth, and it merged into one. ॥11॥
2.12: There the gods saw a mass of intense radiance like a blazing mountain, its flames pervading the spaces between the quarters. ॥12॥
2.13: That matchless radiance, born from the bodies of all the gods, gathered in one place and became a woman, pervading the three worlds with her lustre. ॥13॥
2.14: The radiance that was Śambhu’s became her face; from Yama’s came her hair, and her arms from the radiance of Viṣṇu. ॥14॥
2.15: From the Moon’s radiance came the pair of breasts, from Indra’s the waist, from Varuṇa’s the shanks and thighs, and the hips from the radiance of the Earth. ॥15॥
2.16: From Brahmās radiance came the feet, and their toes from the Sun’s radiance; from that of the Vasus the fingers, and from Kubera’s the nose. ॥16॥
2.17: Her teeth arose from the radiance of Prajāpati, and likewise her three eyes were born from the radiance of Fire. ॥17॥
2.18: Her brows were the radiance of the two twilights, and her ears that of the Wind; and from the radiances of the other gods too came the birth of the auspicious Devī (Śivā). ॥18॥
2.19: Then, beholding her who had arisen from the mass of radiance of all the gods, the immortals oppressed by Mahiṣa were filled with joy. Then the gods gave her each his own weapon. ॥19॥
2.20: The wielder of the Pināka (Śiva) drew forth a trident from his own trident and gave it to her; and Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu) gave a discus, bringing it forth from his own discus. ॥20॥
2.21: Varuṇa gave her a conch, and Agni (the oblation-eater) a spear; Māruta (the Wind) gave a bow and likewise two quivers full of arrows. ॥21॥
2.22: Indra, lord of the immortals, the thousand-eyed, brought forth a thunderbolt from his own thunderbolt and gave it to her, and a bell from the elephant Airāvata. ॥22॥
2.23: Yama gave a staff from his staff of Death, and the lord of waters (Varuṇa) a noose; Prajāpati gave a rosary, and Brahmā a water-pot. ॥23॥
2.24: The Sun placed his own rays in all the pores of her skin, and Kāla gave her a sword and a spotless shield. ॥24॥
2.25: The Ocean of Milk gave a spotless necklace and likewise a pair of never-aging garments, a divine crest-jewel, a pair of earrings and bracelets, ॥25॥
2.26: a bright crescent-moon ornament, armlets for all her arms, likewise a pair of shining anklets, a peerless necklet, ॥26॥
2.27: and jewelled rings on all her fingers. Viśvakarmā gave her an exceedingly bright axe, ॥27॥
2.28: missiles of many forms, and impenetrable armour. A garland of unfading lotuses for her head and another for her breast ॥28॥
2.29: the Ocean gave her, and a most beautiful lotus. Himavān gave a lion as her mount and various jewels. ॥29॥
2.30: The Lord of Wealth gave a drinking cup never empty of wine. And Śeṣa, lord of all serpents, gave adorned with great gems ॥30॥
2.31: a serpent-necklace — he who bears this earth gave it to her. Honoured likewise by the other gods with ornaments and weapons, the Devī ॥31॥
2.32: so honoured, roared aloud with a loud laugh again and again. By her terrible roar the whole sky was filled. ॥32॥
2.33: From that immeasurable, exceedingly great roar a mighty echo arose. All the worlds were shaken and the oceans trembled. ॥33॥
2.34: The earth quaked and all the mountains shook. And the gods joyfully cried to her, the lion-rider, ‘Victory!’ ॥34॥
2.35: And the sages, their bodies bowed in devotion, praised her. Seeing the entire three worlds agitated, the enemies of the gods ॥35॥
2.36: they, with all their armies equipped, rose up with weapons raised. ‘Ah! What is this?’ crying out in anger, Mahiṣāsura ॥36॥
2.37: rushed towards that sound, surrounded by all the asuras. Then he saw the Devī, pervading the three worlds with her radiance, ॥37॥
2.38: her who made the earth bend under the tread of her feet, whose crown grazed the sky, who shook all the netherworlds with the twang of her bowstring, ॥38॥
2.39: standing with her thousand arms pervading the directions all around. Then began the battle of the enemies of the gods with that Devī, ॥39॥
2.40: a battle in which the spaces between the quarters were set ablaze by weapons and missiles hurled in many ways. Mahiṣāsura’s general, the great asura named Cikṣura, ॥40॥
2.41: fought, and Cāmara too, with others, accompanied by a fourfold army. The great asura named Udagra, with sixty thousand chariots, ॥41॥
2.42: fought; and Mahāhanu with a thousand ayutas ten million; and the great asura Asiloman with fifty niyutas, ॥42॥
2.43: and Bāṣkala fought in the battle with six hundred ayutas. Surrounded by many multitudes of thousands of elephants and horses, ॥43॥
2.44: and encompassed by a crore of chariots, he fought in that battle. And Biḍāla, with fifty ayutas of ayutas, ॥44॥
2.45: of chariots, surrounded by them, fought there in the conflict. And others there, encompassed by chariots, elephants and horses in tens of thousands, ॥45॥
2.46: the great asuras fought there in the conflict with the Devī. And with thousands of crores upon crores of chariots, of elephants likewise, ॥46॥
2.47: and of horses, surrounded by them, Mahiṣāsura was there in the battle. With javelins and bhindipālas, with spears and maces likewise, ॥47॥
2.48: with swords, axes and paṭṭiśas they fought with the Devī in the conflict. Some hurled spears, and others likewise nooses. ॥48॥
2.49: They began to strike that Devī with blows of their swords. Then that Devī Caṇḍikā, in turn, cut down those weapons and missiles… ॥49॥
2.50: …cut to pieces as if in mere play, herself raining down her own weapons and missiles; the Devī, her face untroubled, being praised by the gods and sages, ॥50॥
2.51: the Sovereign Devī hurled weapons and missiles into the bodies of the asuras. And the lion, the Devī’s mount, enraged and shaking its mane, ॥51॥
2.52: ranged through the asura armies like a fire through forests. And the breaths that Ambikā exhaled while fighting in the battle— ॥52॥
2.53: those very breaths at once became troops of attendants by hundreds of thousands. They fought with axes, bhindipālas, swords and paṭṭiśas, ॥53॥
2.54: destroying the hosts of asuras, strengthened by the power of the Devī. Some of the attendants beat drums, and others blew conches, ॥54॥
2.55: and others likewise played mṛdaṅgas at that great festival of battle. Then the Devī, with her trident, her mace, showers of spears, ॥55॥
2.56: and with sword and the rest, slew the great asuras by hundreds; and she felled others who were stupefied by the sound of her bell. ॥56॥
2.57: Binding other asuras with her noose, she dragged them along the ground. Some were cut in two by sharp strokes of the sword; and others, ॥57॥
2.58: crushed by the fall of her mace, lie on the ground. And some, badly struck by the pestle, vomited blood. ॥58॥
2.59: Some fell to the ground, pierced in the chest by the trident. Some on the battlefield were riddled through by a flood of arrows, ॥59॥
2.60: and, swooping like hawks, those tormentors of the gods gave up their lives. Of some the arms were cut off; others likewise had their necks severed. ॥60॥
2.61: The heads of others fell; others were split through the middle; and still other great asuras, their legs cut off, fell to the earth. ॥61॥
2.62: Some, split in two by the Devī, were left with one arm, one eye and one foot. And others, even with their heads cut off, fell and rose up again. ॥62॥
2.63: Headless trunks, grasping their finest weapons, fought with the Devī; and others there in the battle danced, keeping to the rhythm of the war-music. ॥63॥
2.64: Other great asuras, headless trunks with heads cut off, sword, spear and lance in hand, kept crying to the Devī, “Stop! Stop!” ॥64॥
2.65: With fallen chariots, elephants, horses and asuras, the earth became impassable there where that great battle took place. ॥65॥
2.66: There, at once, great rivers of streaming blood flowed forth in the midst of the asura army, made from the blood of elephants, asuras and horses. ॥66॥
2.67: In a moment Ambikā brought that great army of the asuras to destruction, just as fire destroys a great heap of grass and wood. ॥67॥
2.68: And that lion, letting out a mighty roar and shaking its mane, seemed to be searching out the life-breaths from the bodies of the enemies of the gods. ॥68॥
2.69: There the Devī’s attendants fought such a battle with the asuras that the gods in heaven, showering flowers, were delighted with them. ॥69॥
2.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the second adhyāya, named the slaying of Mahiṣāsura’s army. ॥2॥
3.dhyana: Om. I worship the Devī who shines with the radiance of a thousand rising suns, who wears red silk and a garland of heads, whose breasts are smeared with blood, who holds in her lotus-like hands a rosary, knowledge the book, the gesture of fearlessness and the gesture of boon-giving, whose lotus face glows with three eyes, whose crown is set with jewels and the moon, and who is seated on a lotus.
3.2: Seeing that army being slaughtered, the great asura Cikṣura, the commander, then advanced in anger to fight Ambikā. ॥2॥
3.3: In the battle that asura rained a shower of arrows on the Devī, as a cloud rains a shower of water on the peak of Mount Meru. ॥3॥
3.4: Then the Devī, cutting down his masses of arrows as if in play, slew his horses with arrows, and the driver of the horses as well. ॥4॥
3.5: And at once she cut his bow and his very lofty banner, and with swift arrows she pierced him, his bow cut, in the limbs. ॥5॥
3.6: That asura, his bow cut, chariotless, his horses slain, his charioteer slain, rushed at the Devī holding sword and shield. ॥6॥
3.7: With his keen-edged sword he struck the lion on the head and, very swift, struck the Devī too on her left arm. ॥7॥
3.8: His sword, on reaching her arm, shattered, O prince. Then he, his eyes red with anger, seized a spear. ॥8॥
3.9: And then the great asura hurled it at Bhadrakālī, blazing with radiance like the sun’s disc falling from the sky. ॥9॥
3.10: Seeing that spear falling upon her, the Devī released her own spear; by it that spear was shattered into a hundred pieces, and so was the great asura. ॥10॥
3.11: When that mighty commander of Mahiṣa’s army was slain, Cāmara, the tormentor of the gods, came mounted on an elephant. ॥11॥
3.12: He too then hurled a śakti-spear at the Devī; Ambikā swiftly struck it down with a roar of ‘huṃ’ and made it fall to the ground, lustreless. ॥12॥
3.13: Seeing the śakti broken and fallen, Cāmara, filled with rage, hurled a trident; that too she cut down with arrows. ॥13॥
3.14: Then the lion leapt up and, settling between the elephant’s frontal globes, fought fiercely in close combat with that enemy of the gods. ॥14॥
3.15: Then the two, fighting, came down from that elephant to the ground, and fought on, greatly enraged, with most terrible blows. ॥15॥
3.16: Then the lion, springing swiftly into the sky and swooping down, severed Cāmara’s head with a blow of its paw. ॥16॥
3.17: And Udagra was slain in battle by the Devī with stones, trees and the like; and Karāla too was struck down with teeth, fists and slaps. ॥17॥
3.18: The enraged Devī crushed Uddhata with blows of her mace, Bāṣkala with a javelin, and Tāmra and Andhaka with arrows. ॥18॥
3.19: And the three-eyed Supreme Devī slew Ugrāsya, Ugravīrya and likewise Mahāhanu with her trident. ॥19॥
3.20: With her sword she struck Biḍāla’s head from his body, and with arrows she sent both Durdhara and Durmukha to the abode of Yama. ॥20॥
3.21: As his own army was thus being destroyed, Mahiṣāsura terrified those troops of the Devī in his buffalo form. ॥21॥
3.22: Some by blows of his muzzle, others likewise by stamping of his hooves, others lashed by his tail, and others torn apart by his two horns — ॥22॥
3.23: some others by his charge, by his bellowing and by his whirling, and others by the blast of his breath, he felled to the ground. ॥23॥
3.24: Having felled the host of her attendants, that asura rushed forward to kill the lion of the Great Devī. Then Ambikā grew angry. ॥24॥
3.25: He too, of great might, in his anger trampled the surface of the earth with his hooves, flung high mountains with his two horns and bellowed. ॥25॥
3.26: Crushed by his swift circling, the earth was shattered; and the ocean, lashed by his tail, overflowed on every side. ॥26॥
3.27: Torn apart by his tossing horns, the clouds went to pieces; and mountains, flung by the wind of his breath, fell from the sky by hundreds. ॥27॥
3.28: Seeing the great asura thus swollen with rage and rushing at her, Caṇḍikā then grew wrathful for his slaying. ॥28॥
3.29: She cast her noose over him and bound that great asura. Bound thus in the great battle, he abandoned his buffalo form. ॥29॥
3.30: Then he instantly became a lion. Just as Ambikā was cutting off its head, a man with sword in hand appeared. ॥30॥
3.31: At once the Devī cut down that man with her arrows, together with his sword and shield. Then he became a great elephant. ॥31॥
3.32: With his trunk he dragged the great lion of the Devī and trumpeted; but as he was dragging, the Devī cut off his trunk with her sword. ॥32॥
3.33: Then the great asura took on his buffalo body once more and, as before, threw the three worlds with all moving and unmoving beings into turmoil. ॥33॥
3.34: Then Caṇḍikā, Mother of the world, enraged, drank the supreme drink again and again and laughed, her eyes turned red. ॥34॥
3.35: And the asura too, puffed up with the pride of his strength and valour, roared, and with his horns hurled mountains at Caṇḍikā. ॥35॥
3.36: And she, pulverizing with showers of arrows those mountains hurled by him, spoke to him in words faltering from the flush that the elation of the drink had brought to her face. ॥36॥
3.38: Roar, roar for a moment, fool, while I drink this honey-wine. When you are slain by me right here, the gods will soon be roaring in joy. ॥38॥
3.40: Having spoken thus, she sprang up and mounted that great asura; pressing his neck down with her foot, she struck him with her trident. ॥40॥
3.41: Then he, trodden underfoot by her, came only half-way out of his own mouth, held fast by the power of the Devī. ॥41॥
3.42: Still fighting while only half emerged, that great asura was felled by the Devī, who cut off his head with her great sword. ॥42॥
3.43: Then the whole daitya army, crying out in dismay, perished; and all the hosts of the gods attained supreme joy. ॥43॥
3.44: The gods, together with the celestial great sages, praised that Devī; the lords of the gandharvas sang and the troupes of apsarases danced. ॥44॥
3.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the third adhyāya, named the slaying of Mahiṣāsura. ॥3॥
4.dhyana: Om. One should meditate on Durgā called Jayā, whose lustre is like a dark cloud, who with her side-glances strikes fear into the hosts of enemies, who wears the crescent moon bound on her crown, who holds in her hands a conch, a discus, a sword and also a trident, who has three eyes, who is mounted on the shoulders of a lion, who fills the entire three worlds with her radiance, who is surrounded by the gods and served by those who seek spiritual attainments.
4.2: When that exceedingly mighty, evil-souled one and the army of the enemies of the gods had been slain by the Devī, Śakra and the hosts of gods praised her with words, their necks and shoulders bent low in reverence, their bodies beautiful with hair standing on end from joy. ॥2॥
4.3: To that Ambikā, worthy of worship by all gods and great sages, the Devī who by her own power has pervaded this world and whose form is the aggregate of the powers of all the hosts of gods, we bow in devotion. May she bestow auspicious things on us. ॥3॥
4.4: Whose incomparable glory and might neither the blessed Ananta, nor Brahmā, nor Hara is able to describe — may that Caṇḍikā set her mind on protecting the whole world and on destroying the fear of evil. ॥4॥
4.5: You who are yourself Fortune (Śrī) in the homes of the virtuous, Misfortune (Alakṣmī) in those of the sinful, intelligence in the hearts of the wise, faith in the good, modesty in one born of a noble family — to you we bow. O Devī, protect the universe. ॥5॥
4.6: How shall we describe this inconceivable form of yours? Or your exceeding, abundant valour that destroys the asuras? Or those deeds of yours in battles that surpass all others, O Devī, among all the hosts of asuras, gods and the rest? ॥6॥
4.7: You are the cause of all the worlds; though composed of the three guṇas, you are not known to be touched by their defects; you are unfathomable even to Hari, Hara and the others. You are the refuge of all; this whole world is a portion of you. For you are the unmanifest, supreme, primordial Prakṛti. ॥7॥
4.8: O Devī, you are indeed Svāhā, by the utterance of whom the entire assembly of gods attains satisfaction in all sacrifices; and you are the cause of satisfaction of the hosts of ancestors; therefore you are uttered by people as Svadhā too. ॥8॥
4.9: O Devī, you who are the cause of liberation, whose great vows are beyond thought, who are practised by sages seeking liberation, who have well-restrained senses, who hold to the essence of truth and have cast off all faults — you are that blessed supreme Knowledge (Vidyā). ॥9॥
4.10: You are of the nature of sound, the repository of the very pure Ṛk and Yajus and of the Sāmans with their lovely recitation of words in the Udgītha. O Devī, you are the blessed Trayī (the three Vedas); you are Vārtā (livelihood) for the sustenance of existence; you are the supreme remover of the afflictions of all the worlds. ॥10॥
4.11: O Devī, you are Medhā (intellect), who know the essence of all scriptures; you are Durgā, the boat across the hard-to-cross ocean of worldly existence, free of attachment; you are Śrī, who has made her sole abode in the heart of Kaiṭabha’s foe (Viṣṇu); you alone are Gaurī, established with the moon-crested one (Śiva). ॥11॥
4.12: Having seen your face — slightly smiling, spotless, resembling the disc of the full moon, lovely with the lustre of the finest gold — it is most wonderful that Mahiṣāsura, seized by anger, nevertheless suddenly struck at it. ॥12॥
4.13: But, O Devī, that Mahiṣa, having seen your face angry, terrible with knitted brows, its colour like the rising moon, did not give up his life at once — that is very strange. For who can live after seeing Death enraged? ॥13॥
4.14: O Devī, be gracious. You, the Supreme, exist for the world’s well-being; when angry you instantly destroy whole races. This was known just now, when this vast army of Mahiṣāsura was brought to its end. ॥14॥
4.15: Those on whom you, the giver of prosperity, are always pleased are honoured in their lands; theirs is wealth, theirs is fame; their circle of kin does not suffer; they alone are blessed, with obedient sons, servants and wives. ॥15॥
4.16: O Devī, the virtuous person, with great reverence, performs all righteous deeds daily, and thereby goes to heaven through your grace. Therefore, O Devī, are you not the giver of fruits in all three worlds? ॥16॥
4.17: O Durgā, when remembered you take away the fear of every creature; when remembered by those at ease you grant a mind exceedingly auspicious. O remover of poverty, sorrow and fear, who other than you has a heart ever tender for doing good to all? ॥17॥
4.18: “By the slaying of these, the world attains happiness; and though these may have committed sin to earn hell for a long time, let them attain death in battle and go to heaven” — thinking thus, surely, O Devī, you slay the enemies. ॥18॥
4.19: Why do you not reduce all the asuras to ashes by a mere glance? That you hurl weapons at the enemies is because you think: “Let even the foes, purified by the weapons, go to the higher worlds.” Such is your benevolent intent even towards those hostile ones. ॥19॥
4.20: That the eyes of the asuras were not destroyed by the fierce flashing of the masses of light from your sword and by the abundant lustre of your trident’s point — that is because they were gazing on your face, which bears the radiant crescent moon. ॥20॥
4.21: O Devī, your nature is to subdue the conduct of the wicked; and this form of yours is inconceivable and unequalled by others; and your valour destroys those who robbed the gods of their prowess. Thus you have shown compassion even towards enemies. ॥21॥
4.22: With what can this prowess of yours be compared? And where is there a form like yours, exceedingly captivating yet striking fear into enemies? Compassion in the heart and relentlessness in battle are seen, O boon-giving Devī, in you alone in all the three worlds. ॥22॥
4.23: This entire triple world has been saved by you through the destruction of the foes; having slain the hosts of enemies at the forefront of battle, you have led even them to heaven; and our fear arising from the frenzied enemies of the gods has been dispelled. Salutations to you. ॥23॥
4.24: O Devī, protect us with your spear; O Ambikā, protect us with your sword; protect us with the sound of your bell and with the twang of your bowstring. ॥24॥
4.25: Protect us in the east and in the west, O Caṇḍikā; protect us in the south, and likewise in the north, O Īśvarī, by whirling your own trident. ॥25॥
4.26: Those gentle forms of yours that roam the three worlds, and those that are exceedingly terrible: with them protect us and likewise the earth. ॥26॥
4.27: O Ambikā, the weapons of yours, sword, trident, mace and the rest, which rest in your tender hands: with them protect us on every side. ॥27॥
4.29: Thus praised by the gods, the Sustainer of the worlds was worshipped with divine flowers grown in the Nandana garden, and likewise with perfumes and unguents. ॥29॥
4.30: Devoutly perfumed with divine incense by all the gods, she, her face bright with grace, spoke to all the gods bowed before her. ॥30॥
4.32: O gods, all of you, let whatever you desire from me be chosen. ॥32॥
4.34: Everything has been accomplished by the Blessed Devī; nothing remains. ॥34॥
4.35: since this enemy of ours, Mahiṣāsura, has been slain. And yet, if a boon is to be given to us by you, O Maheśvarī, ॥35॥
4.36: whenever you are remembered, may you destroy our gravest calamities. And, O you of spotless face, the mortal who will praise you with these hymns— ॥36॥
4.37: for his increase in wealth, prosperity and splendour, and in fortunes such as riches and wife, may you, pleased with us, always be favourable, O Ambikā. ॥37॥
4.39: Thus propitiated by the gods for the sake of the world and of themselves, Bhadrakālī said “So be it” and vanished, O king. ॥39॥
4.40: Thus I have told you, O king, how in former times that Devī, who desires the welfare of the three worlds, arose from the bodies of the gods. ॥40॥
4.41: And again, how she arose from the body of Gaurī, for the slaying of the wicked Daityas and of Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥41॥
4.42: and for the protection of the worlds, as the benefactress of the gods: hear that as told by me; I shall narrate it to you exactly as it happened. ॥42॥
4.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the fourth adhyāya, named the praise by Śakra and the gods. ॥4॥
5.viniyoga: Of this sacred Uttara Caritra (the Final Episode), Rudra is the seer, Śrī Mahāsarasvatī is the deity, Anuṣṭubh is the metre, Bhīmā is the power, Bhrāmarī is the seed, the Sun is the principle, and the Sāmaveda is its form. Its application is in the recitation of the Uttara Caritra, for the pleasing of Śrī Mahāsarasvatī.
5.dhyana: Here I worship Mahāsarasvatī, who holds in her lotus-hands bell, trident, plough, conch, pestle, discus, bow and arrow; whose radiance equals that of the moon shining at the end of the cloudy season; who arose from the body of Gaurī; who is the support of the three worlds; and who destroys the demons Śumbha and the rest.
5.1: Om klīṃ. The sage Medhas said: ॥1॥
5.2: Long ago the two asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha, relying on their pride and strength, seized from the lord of Śacī Indra the three worlds and his shares of the sacrifice. ॥2॥
5.3: Those two likewise took over the office of the Sun, and in the same way that of the Moon, of Kubera, of Yama, and of Varuṇa. ॥3॥
5.4: Those two also took over the power of Vāyu and the function of Agni. Then the gods, defeated and fallen from their sovereignty, were driven out. ॥4॥
5.5: All the gods, stripped of their offices and cast out by those two great asuras, called to mind that invincible Devī. ॥5॥
5.6: They thought: ‘She granted us a boon: “When remembered in times of calamity, I will at that very moment destroy all your gravest misfortunes.”’ ॥6॥
5.7: Having resolved thus, the gods went to Himavat, lord of mountains, and there they praised the Devī, Viṣṇumāyā. ॥7॥
5.9: Salutation to the Devī, to the Great Devī; to Śivā, the auspicious one, salutation always. Salutation to Prakṛti, to Bhadrā, the gracious one. Self-controlled, we bow to her. ॥9॥
5.10: Salutation to the Fierce One, to the Eternal One; to Gaurī, to the Sustainer, salutations again and again. To her who is moonlight and has the form of the moon, to her who is happiness, salutation always. ॥10॥
5.11: To the Auspicious One, to the prosperity and success of those who bow, we offer salutations again and again. To Nairṛtī, to the fortune (Lakṣmī) of kings, to Śarvāṇī — to you, salutations again and again. ॥11॥
5.12: To Durgā, to her who carries us across difficulties, to the Essence, to the Doer of all, to Khyāti (Fame), and likewise to Kṛṣṇā, the dark one, and to Dhūmrā, the smoky one — salutation always. ॥12॥
5.13: We bow to her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce; to her, salutations again and again. Salutation to the Devī who is the foundation of the world, to Kṛti (Action), salutations again and again. ॥13॥
5.14: Salutation to the Devī who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā. ॥14॥
5.16: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥16॥
5.17: Salutation to the Devī who in all beings is called consciousness. ॥17॥
5.19: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥19॥
5.20: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as intelligence. ॥20॥
5.22: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥22॥
5.23: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as sleep. ॥23॥
5.25: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥25॥
5.26: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as hunger. ॥26॥
5.28: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥28॥
5.29: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as shadow. ॥29॥
5.31: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥31॥
5.32: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as power. ॥32॥
5.34: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥34॥
5.35: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as thirst. ॥35॥
5.37: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥37॥
5.38: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as forbearance. ॥38॥
5.40: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥40॥
5.41: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as birth. ॥41॥
5.43: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥43॥
5.44: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as modesty. ॥44॥
5.46: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥46॥
5.47: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as peace. ॥47॥
5.49: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥49॥
5.50: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as faith. ॥50॥
5.52: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥52॥
5.53: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as beauty. ॥53॥
5.55: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥55॥
5.56: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as fortune. ॥56॥
5.58: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥58॥
5.59: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as livelihood. ॥59॥
5.61: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥61॥
5.62: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as memory. ॥62॥
5.64: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥64॥
5.65: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as compassion. ॥65॥
5.67: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥67॥
5.68: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as contentment. ॥68॥
5.70: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥70॥
5.71: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as mother. ॥71॥
5.73: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥73॥
5.74: Salutation to the Devī who abides in all beings as delusion. ॥74॥
5.76: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥76॥
5.77: She who presides over the senses of beings and who constantly pervades all beings: to that all-pervading Devī, salutation, salutation. ॥77॥
5.78: Salutation to her who, as consciousness, pervades this whole world and abides in it. ॥78॥
5.80: Salutation to her, salutation again and again. ॥80॥
5.81: Praised of old by the gods for the sake of attaining what they desired, and likewise served day after day by the lord of the gods, may that Sovereign Devī, the cause of good, bring about auspicious and blessed things for us, and destroy our calamities. ॥81॥
5.82: She, the Ruler, who is now being bowed to by us gods tormented by the arrogant Daityas, and who, when remembered by us with bodies bowed in devotion, destroys all our calamities at that very moment— may she do us good. ॥82॥
5.84: While the gods were thus engaged in praise there, Pārvatī came to bathe in the water of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), O son of a king. ॥84॥
5.85: She of lovely brows said to those gods, “Who is being praised by you here?” And Śivā, emerging from the sheath of her body, said: ॥85॥
5.86: “This hymn to me is being made by the assembled gods, who have been spurned by the Daitya Śumbha and defeated in battle by Niśumbha.” ॥86॥
5.87: Because Ambikā came forth from the bodily sheath (kośa) of that Pārvatī, she is therefore sung of in all the worlds as Kauśikī. ॥87॥
5.88: When she had come forth, that Pārvatī too became dark, and, having made the Himālaya her abode, became known as Kālikā. ॥88॥
5.89: Then Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the servants of Śumbha and Niśumbha, saw Ambikā bearing a supreme, most enchanting form. ॥89॥
5.90: And she was reported by the two to Śumbha: O great king, some woman of exceeding charm is dwelling there, illuminating the Himālaya. ॥90॥
5.91: Never has such a supreme beauty been seen anywhere by anyone. Let it be found out who this goddess is, and let her be seized, O lord of the Asuras. ॥91॥
5.92: A jewel among women, of exceedingly lovely limbs, lighting up the directions with her radiance—she is staying there, O lord of the Daityas; you ought to see her. ॥92॥
5.93: O lord, whatever jewels, gems, elephants, horses and the like there are in the three worlds, all of them now shine in your house. ॥93॥
5.94: Airāvata, the jewel among elephants, has been brought from Purandara; so too this Pārijāta tree, and likewise the horse Uccaiḥśravas. ॥94॥
5.95: This aerial chariot yoked with swans stands in your courtyard; it has been brought here, a jewel, the wondrous one that belonged to Vedhas (Brahmā). ॥95॥
5.96: This treasure Mahāpadma has been brought from the lord of wealth (Kubera); and the ocean gave a garland of unfading lotuses, rich with filaments. ॥96॥
5.97: In your house stands Varuṇa’s umbrella that streams gold; likewise this finest chariot, which formerly belonged to Prajāpati. ॥97॥
5.98: O lord, the spear of Death named Utkrāntidā has been seized by you; the noose of the king of waters (Varuṇa) is in your brother’s possession. ॥98॥
5.99: And all kinds of gems born of the ocean belong to Niśumbha; Fire too gave you two garments purified by fire. ॥99॥
5.100: Thus, O lord of the Daityas, all jewels have been brought to you by you. Why is this auspicious lady, a jewel among women, not taken by you? ॥100॥
5.102: Having heard these words of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Śumbha then sent the great asura Sugrīva as messenger to the Devī. ॥102॥
5.103: Śumbha said: Go and tell her thus and thus on my word; and act quickly in such a way that she comes with gladness. ॥103॥
5.104: He went there, to where she was staying in a very beautiful mountain region, and then spoke gently to the Devī in a sweet voice. ॥104॥
5.106: O Devī, Śumbha, lord of the Daityas, is the supreme lord in the three worlds. I am a messenger sent by him, and have come here into your presence. ॥106॥
5.107: He whose command is ever unobstructed among all classes of divine beings, who has conquered all the enemies of the Daityas — hear what he has said. ॥107॥
5.108: The whole of the three worlds is mine; the gods are obedient to my will; I alone enjoy all the shares of the sacrifices, each one separately. ॥108॥
5.109: The choicest jewels in the three worlds are wholly in my power; likewise the jewel among elephants, the mount of the king of the gods, has been taken. ॥109॥
5.110: The jewel among horses named Uccaiḥśravas, which arose from the churning of the milk ocean, was offered to me by the immortals bowing down. ॥110॥
5.111: And whatever other beings that are jewels of their kind exist among the gods, gandharvas and serpents, they are with me alone, O beautiful one. ॥111॥
5.112: O Devī, we regard you as the jewel among women in the world. Such as you are, come to us, for we are the enjoyers of jewels. ॥112॥
5.113: Accept either me or my younger brother Niśumbha of mighty valour, O you of restless glances, since you are indeed a jewel. ॥113॥
5.114: By becoming my wife you will attain supreme, unequalled sovereignty. Reflecting on this with your understanding, become my wife. ॥114॥
5.116: Thus addressed, the Devī, smiling deeply within, then spoke — Durgā, the blessed and auspicious one, by whom this world is upheld. ॥116॥
5.118: What you have said is true; nothing you have spoken here is false. Śumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Niśumbha too is of the same kind. ॥118॥
5.119: But in this matter, how can what I have vowed be made false? Hear the vow that I made long ago out of my little understanding. ॥119॥
5.120: “Whoever defeats me in battle, whoever takes away my pride, whoever is equal to me in strength in the world, he will be my husband.” ॥120॥
5.121: So let Śumbha come here, or the mighty Niśumbha. Having conquered me here, why delay? Let him quickly take my hand in marriage. ॥121॥
5.123: You are arrogant; O Devī, do not speak thus before me. In the three worlds, what man could stand before Śumbha and Niśumbha? ॥123॥
5.124: Not even all the gods can stand in battle face to face with the other Daityas, O Devī; how much less you, a woman, all alone? ॥124॥
5.125: Śumbha and the others, before whom all the gods led by Indra could not stand in battle — how will you, a woman, go to face them? ॥125॥
5.126: So, told by me, you go to the side of Śumbha and Niśumbha; do not go with your dignity ruined by being dragged by the hair. ॥126॥
5.128: So it is: Śumbha is mighty, and Niśumbha too is such. What can I do, since my vow was made long ago without reflection? ॥128॥
5.129: So go, and respectfully report to the lord of the asuras everything I have told you; and let him do what is fitting. ॥129॥
5.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the fifth adhyāya, named the dialogue of the Devī and the messenger. ॥5॥
6.dhyana: Om. I meditate on Padmāvatī, whose seat is the lord of serpents; whose slender, creeper-like body shines with a large string of gems that serve as ornaments on the serpents hoods; who is like the sun and radiant with three eyes; whose hands hold a rosary, a pitcher, a skull and a lotus; who wears the half-moon as her crest; the supreme one, who dwells in the body of Bhairava, the all-knowing Lord.
6.2: Having heard these words of the Devī, the messenger, filled with indignation, went back and reported them in full detail to the king of the Daityas. ॥2॥
6.3: Then, having heard that report of the messenger, the king of the Asuras, enraged, spoke to Dhūmralocana, a chief of the Daityas: ॥3॥
6.4: O Dhūmralocana, quickly, surrounded by your own army, bring that wicked woman here by force, distraught as she is dragged by her hair. ॥4॥
6.5: If anyone else rises up to give her protection, he must be slain, be he an immortal god, a Yakṣa or a Gandharva. ॥5॥
6.7: Thus commanded by him, the Daitya Dhūmralocana at once set out swiftly, surrounded by sixty thousand Asuras. ॥7॥
6.8: Then, seeing the Devī stationed on the snowy mountain, he cried aloud: Come to the presence of Śumbha and Niśumbha! ॥8॥
6.9: If you do not come to my master willingly today, then I will take you by force, distraught as you are dragged by your hair. ॥9॥
6.11: “Sent by the lord of the Daityas, mighty yourself and surrounded by an army, if you take me by force in this way, then what can I do to you?” ॥11॥
6.13: Thus addressed, the Asura Dhūmralocana rushed at her; then Ambikā reduced him to ashes with merely the sound “huṃ”. ॥13॥
6.14: Then Ambikā rained sharp arrows, as well as spears and axes, upon the enraged great army of the Asuras. ॥14॥
6.15: Then the lion, the Devī’s own mount, shaking its mane in fury and letting out a most terrible roar, fell upon the army of the Asuras. ॥15॥
6.16: Some Daityas he slew with blows of his paws, others with his mouth, and other great Asuras by trampling and with his jaws. ॥16॥
6.17: The maned lion tore open the bellies of some with his claws, and with blows of his paw he severed others heads from their bodies. ॥17॥
6.18: Others he left with arms and heads cut off; and, shaking his mane, he drank the blood from the bellies of yet others. ॥18॥
6.19: In a moment that whole army was brought to destruction by that mighty lion, the Devī’s mount, in his exceeding wrath. ॥19॥
6.20: Hearing that the Asura Dhūmralocana had been slain by the Devī, and that his whole army had then been destroyed by the Devī’s lion, ॥20॥
6.21: Śumbha, the overlord of the Daityas, became furious, his lip quivering, and he commanded the two great Asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa: ॥21॥
6.22: O Caṇḍa, O Muṇḍa! Surrounded by many troops, go there, and having gone, let her be brought here quickly, ॥22॥
6.23: dragging her by the hair or binding her. If you have any doubt of success in battle, then let her be slain by all the Asuras with every weapon. ॥23॥
6.24: When that wicked woman has been slain and the lion struck down, come back quickly — or else bind and seize that Ambikā and bring her. ॥24॥
6.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the sixth adhyāya, named the slaying of Dhūmralocana, general of Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥6॥
7.dhyana: Om. I would meditate on Mātaṅgī: seated on a jewelled throne, listening to the sweet sounds recited by a parrot, dark-limbed, with one foot placed on a lotus, bearing a digit of the moon, playing the vīṇā, wearing a garland bound of kalhāra lilies, with a close-fitting shining bodice, clad in jewelled garments, holding a conch-shell cup, intoxicated with sweet wine, her forehead radiant with a tilaka mark.
7.2: Then, so commanded, those Daityas, led by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, accompanied by a fourfold army, marched forth with weapons raised. ॥2॥
7.3: Then they saw the Devī, gently smiling, seated upon the lion on a great golden peak of the lord of mountains. ॥3॥
7.4: Seeing her, they, eager, made an effort to seize her; and others, with bows drawn and swords in hand, came near her. ॥4॥
7.5: Then Ambikā became fiercely angry with those enemies, and from her anger her face then turned black as ink. ॥5॥
7.6: From her forehead, contorted by a frown, there swiftly sprang forth Kālī, of terrible face, armed with sword and noose. ॥6॥
7.7: She bore a strange skull-topped staff, was adorned with a garland of human heads, clothed in a tiger-skin, gaunt with withered flesh, exceedingly dreadful. ॥7॥
7.8: Her mouth gaped very wide, she was fearsome with lolling tongue, her eyes were sunken and red, and she filled the quarters with her roar. ॥8॥
7.9: Rushing upon them with speed and slaying the great Asuras, she devoured that host there in the army of the gods enemies. ॥9॥
7.10: Seizing with one hand the elephants, together with their rear-guards, goad-bearing drivers, warriors and bells, she hurled them into her mouth. ॥10॥
7.11: Likewise, putting a warrior with his horses and a chariot with its charioteer into her mouth, she chewed them most dreadfully with her teeth. ॥11॥
7.12: She seized one by the hair, another by the neck; one she trampled under foot, and another she crushed with her chest. ॥12॥
7.13: And the weapons and great missiles discharged by those Asuras she caught with her mouth in fury and ground them to pieces with her teeth. ॥13॥
7.14: That whole host of mighty, evil-minded Asuras she then crushed; some she devoured and others she beat down. ॥14॥
7.15: Some were slain by the sword, some struck by the skull-staff, and others, wounded by the tips of her teeth—thus the Asuras went to destruction. ॥15॥
7.16: Seeing that entire army of the Asuras felled in a moment, Caṇḍa rushed at that exceedingly fearsome Kālī. ॥16॥
7.17: The great Asura Caṇḍa covered that terrible-eyed one with showers of most dreadful arrows, and Muṇḍa with discuses hurled by the thousand. ॥17॥
7.18: Those many discuses, entering her mouth, shone like numerous orbs of the sun entering the belly of a cloud. ॥18॥
7.19: Then Kālī, roaring dreadfully, of terrible face, gleaming with teeth hard to look upon, laughed fearsomely in her extreme wrath. ॥19॥
7.20: Rising up on her great lion, the Devī ran at Caṇḍa, and seizing him by the hair, cut off his head with that sword. ॥20॥
7.21: Then Muṇḍa, seeing Caṇḍa felled, rushed at her; she too, in fury, struck him with the sword and brought him down to the ground. ॥21॥
7.22: Then, seeing Caṇḍa felled and the most mighty Muṇḍa too, the remnant of the army that survived fled in all directions, stricken with fear. ॥22॥
7.23: And Kālī, taking the head of Caṇḍa and that of Muṇḍa too, approached Caṇḍikā and spoke, her words mingled with fierce, loud laughter: ॥23॥
7.24: “Here I have brought you Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa as two great sacrificial beasts; in the sacrifice of battle you yourself shall slay Śumbha and Niśumbha.” ॥24॥
7.26: Then, seeing those two great asuras, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, brought before her, the auspicious Caṇḍikā spoke playful words to Kālī: ॥26॥
7.27: “Since you have come bringing Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, you, O Devī, will therefore be renowned in the world as Cāmuṇḍā.” ॥27॥
7.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the seventh adhyāya, named the slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa. ॥7॥
8.dhyana: Om. I contemplate Bhavānī as none other than ‘I’ myself: she who is red like the dawn, whose eyes ripple with waves of compassion, whose hands hold the noose, the goad, the arrows and the bow, and who is surrounded by rays, namely Aṇimā and the other powers.
8.2: When the daitya Caṇḍa had been slain and Muṇḍa struck down, and many armies had been destroyed, the lord of the asuras… ॥2॥
8.3: Then the mighty Śumbha, his mind overpowered by anger, ordered the mobilization of all the armies of the daityas. ॥3॥
8.4: Today let the eighty-six daitya chiefs, with weapons raised, march out with all their forces; let the eighty-four of the Kambus go forth surrounded by their own troops. ॥4॥
8.5: Let the fifty clans of asuras of Koṭivīrya and the hundred clans of the Dhaumras go forth at my command. ॥5॥
8.6: Let the Kālakas, the Daurhṛdas, the Mauryas and likewise the Kālikeya asuras, ready for battle, march out quickly at my command. ॥6॥
8.7: Having given these orders, Śumbha, lord of the asuras, of fearsome command, set out surrounded by many thousands of great armies. ॥7॥
8.8: Seeing that most terrifying army approaching, Caṇḍikā filled the space between earth and sky with the twanging of her bowstring. ॥8॥
8.9: Then, O king, the lion let out an exceedingly great roar, and Ambikā amplified those roars with the sound of her bell. ॥9॥
8.10: Kālī, her mouth opened wide, outdid them all with her terrifying roars, the quarters already being filled with the sound of the bowstring, the lion and the bell. ॥10॥
8.11: Hearing that roar, the enraged daitya armies surrounded the Devī, the lion and Kālī on all four sides. ॥11॥
8.12: Meanwhile, O king, for the destruction of the enemies of the gods and for the well-being of the lions among the immortals, endowed with exceeding valour and strength… ॥12॥
8.13: …the Śaktis of Brahmā, Īśa, Guha and Viṣṇu, and likewise of Indra, emerged from their bodies and went to Caṇḍikā in the forms of those gods. ॥13॥
8.14: Whatever form a god had, and whatever ornaments and mount, in just that way his Śakti came to fight the asuras. ॥14॥
8.15: The Śakti of Brahmā came, seated in a celestial chariot drawn by swans, bearing a rosary and a water-pot; she is called Brahmāṇī. ॥15॥
8.16: Māheśvarī arrived, mounted on a bull, holding an excellent trident, with great serpents as bracelets, and adorned with the crescent moon. ॥16॥
8.17: And Kaumārī, spear in hand, riding the finest peacock, came forward to fight the daityas: Ambikā in the form of Guha. ॥17॥
8.18: Likewise the Śakti Vaiṣṇavī, seated on Garuḍa, came forward holding conch, discus, mace, the Śārṅga bow and sword in her hands. ॥18॥
8.19: The Śakti of Hari, who assumes the incomparable form of the sacrificial Boar, she too came there, bearing a boar’s body. ॥19॥
8.20: Nārasiṃhī, bearing a body like that of Nṛsiṃha, arrived there, scattering the clusters of stars with the tossing of her mane. ॥20॥
8.21: Likewise Aindrī, thunderbolt in hand, seated on the king of elephants, arrived, thousand-eyed; just as Śakra is, so was she. ॥21॥
8.22: Then Īśāna, surrounded by those Śaktis of the gods, said to Caṇḍikā: Let the asuras be slain quickly, for my pleasure. ॥22॥
8.23: Then from the body of the Devī there emerged the Śakti of Caṇḍikā, most terrifying, exceedingly fierce, howling like a hundred jackals. ॥23॥
8.24: And she, the Unvanquished, said to Īśāna of smoky matted hair: O Lord, go you as messenger into the presence of Śumbha and Niśumbha. ॥24॥
8.25: Say to Śumbha and Niśumbha, the two exceedingly arrogant Dānavas, and to the other Dānavas who are assembled there for battle: ॥25॥
8.26: May Indra have the three worlds, and the gods receive the oblations. If you wish to live, go to Pātāla. ॥26॥
8.27: But if, from pride in your strength, you are eager for battle, then come! Let my jackals be sated with your flesh. ॥27॥
8.28: Because Śiva himself was appointed by that Devī to the office of messenger, she became renowned in this world as Śivadūtī. ॥28॥
8.29: Those great asuras too, having heard the Devī’s words as announced by Śarva (Śiva), were filled with fury and went to where Kātyāyanī stood. ॥29॥
8.30: Then, right at the outset, the enemies of the gods, their wrath roused, rained upon that Devī showers of arrows, spears and double-edged swords. ॥30॥
8.31: And she, with great arrows loosed from her twanging bow, playfully cut down those arrows, tridents, spears and axes hurled at her. ॥31॥
8.32: Likewise Kālī then roamed in front of him, rending the foes with the fall of her spear and crushing them with her skull-topped staff. ॥32॥
