8.33: And Brahmāṇī, wherever she rushed, made the enemies bereft of valour and vigour by sprinkling water from her kamaṇḍalu. ॥33॥
8.34: Māheśvarī slew the Daityas with her trident, Vaiṣṇavī likewise with her discus, and Kaumārī, exceedingly wrathful, likewise with her spear. ॥34॥
8.35: Torn apart by the fall of Aindrīs thunderbolt, Daityas and Dānavas by the hundreds fell to the earth, pouring forth streams of blood. ॥35॥
8.36: Shattered by blows of the snout from the boar-form Vārāhī, their chests wounded by the tips of her tusks, and torn by her discus, they fell down. ॥36॥
8.37: Nārasiṃhī roamed the battlefield, devouring other great asuras torn apart by her claws, filling the quarters and the sky with her roar. ॥37॥
8.38: Struck down by Śivadūtīs fierce loud laughter, the asuras fell to the earth; and then she devoured those who had fallen. ॥38॥
8.39: Seeing the enraged host of Mothers thus crushing the great asuras, the soldiers of the gods enemies fled away by various means. ॥39॥
8.40: Seeing the Daityas, harassed by the host of Mothers, intent on flight, the great asura Raktabīja advanced in wrath to fight. ॥40॥
8.41: Whenever a drop of blood falls from his body to the ground, a great asura of his very size springs up from the earth. ॥41॥
8.42: That great asura, mace in hand, fought with Indra’s Śakti; then Aindrī struck Raktabīja with her own thunderbolt. ॥42॥
8.43: From him, struck by the thunderbolt, much blood quickly flowed; from it arose warriors of his form and his prowess. ॥43॥
8.44: As many drops of blood as fell from his body, so many men were born, with his valour, strength and prowess. ॥44॥
8.45: And those men born of the blood also fought there together with the Mothers, a combat most dreadful with the fall of exceedingly fierce weapons. ॥45॥
8.46: And again, when his head was wounded by the stroke of the thunderbolt, blood flowed, and from it men were born by the thousands. ॥46॥
8.47: And Vaiṣṇavī struck him in battle with her discus; Aindrī beat that lord of asuras with a mace. ॥47॥
8.48: The world was pervaded by thousands of great asuras of his size, born from the flow of blood of him who had been pierced by Vaiṣṇavīs discus. ॥48॥
8.49: Kaumārī struck the great asura Raktabīja with her spear, Vārāhī likewise with her sword, and Māheśvarī with her trident. ॥49॥
8.50: And that demon Raktabīja, the great asura, filled with rage, also struck each of the Mothers separately with his mace. ॥50॥
8.51: From him, struck many times by spears, tridents and other weapons, the stream of blood that fell upon the ground—from that, asuras came into being by the hundreds. ॥51॥
8.52: And by those asuras born from the asura’s blood the whole world was pervaded; then the gods fell into the utmost fear. ॥52॥
8.53: Seeing those gods dejected, Caṇḍikā spoke quickly; she said to Kālī: O Cāmuṇḍā, open your mouth wide. ॥53॥
8.54: With this swift mouth, receive the drops of blood arising from the strokes of my weapons, and the great asuras born from the drops of blood. ॥54॥
8.55: Roam the battlefield devouring the great asuras born from it. Thus this demon, his blood drained, will meet destruction. ॥55॥
8.56: “Being devoured by you, the fierce ones will perish, and no others will be born.” Having spoken thus to her, the Devī then struck him with her trident. ॥56॥
8.57: Kālī took Raktabīja’s blood into her mouth. Then he struck Caṇḍikā there with his mace. ॥57॥
8.58: The blow of the mace caused her not even the slightest pain. But from the body of him, struck by her, much blood flowed. ॥58॥
8.59: Wherever it flowed, Cāmuṇḍā received it with her mouth. The great asuras who arose in her mouth from the falling blood— ॥59॥
8.60: —those Cāmuṇḍā devoured, and she drank his blood. The Devī, with trident, thunderbolt, arrows, swords and spears, ॥60॥
8.61: slew that Raktabīja, whose blood had been drunk by Cāmuṇḍā. Struck by the multitude of weapons, he fell upon the surface of the earth. ॥61॥
8.62: And bloodless, O protector of the earth, fell Raktabīja, the great asura. Then the gods, O king, attained incomparable joy. ॥62॥
8.63: The host of Mothers that had arisen from them danced, wild with intoxication from the blood. ॥63॥
8.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the eighth adhyāya, named the slaying of Raktabīja. ॥8॥
9.dhyana: Om. I ceaselessly take refuge in the form that is half Ambikā and half Īśa, whose hue is like the bandhūka flower and gold, who holds with its own staff-like arms a lovely rosary, the noose and the goad, and shows the boon-giving gesture, who has a digit of the moon as an ornament and is three-eyed.
9.2: O revered one, you have told me this wonderful account of the greatness of the Devī’s deeds, concerning the slaying of Raktabīja. ॥2॥
9.3: And I wish to hear further: when Raktabīja had been struck down, what deed did Śumbha do, and the exceedingly wrathful Niśumbha? ॥3॥
9.5: When Raktabīja had been struck down and the others too had been slain in battle, the asura Śumbha and Niśumbha flew into an unequalled rage. ॥5॥
9.6: Then Niśumbha, seeing the great army being slaughtered and carrying his fury, rushed forward with the chief host of the asuras. ॥6॥
9.7: In front of him, likewise behind and on both sides, the great asuras, angry, biting their lips, advanced to kill the Devī. ॥7॥
9.8: Śumbha too, of great valour, surrounded by his own forces, came in anger to slay Caṇḍikā, after fighting with the Mothers. ॥8॥
9.9: Then a fierce battle took place between the Devī and Śumbha and Niśumbha, who loosed an exceedingly terrible rain of arrows like two clouds pouring rain. ॥9॥
9.10: Caṇḍikā cut down the arrows shot by those two with her own masses of arrows, and struck the two lords of the asuras on their limbs with floods of weapons. ॥10॥
9.11: Niśumbha, taking a sharp sword and a gleaming shield, struck on the head the lion, the excellent mount of the Devī. ॥11॥
9.12: When her mount was struck, the Devī swiftly cut with a razor-edged arrow Niśumbha’s excellent sword and also his shield adorned with eight moons. ॥12॥
9.13: When shield and sword were cut, that asura hurled a spear; that too, as it came at her, she split in two with her discus. ॥13॥
9.14: Then the dānava Niśumbha, swollen with rage, seized a trident; as it came, the Devī pulverised it with a blow of her fist. ॥14॥
9.15: Then he, whirling a mace, hurled it at Caṇḍikā; it too, shattered by the Devī’s trident, was reduced to ashes. ॥15॥
9.16: Then, as that bull among daityas came on, axe in hand, the Devī struck him with floods of arrows and felled him to the ground. ॥16॥
9.17: When his brother Niśumbha of terrible prowess had fallen to the earth, Śumbha, exceedingly enraged, set out to kill Ambikā. ॥17॥
9.18: Standing in his chariot, towering high, with his eight matchless arms holding supreme weapons, he shone, pervading the whole sky. ॥18॥
9.19: Seeing him coming, the Devī blew her conch, and also made the twang of her bowstring, exceedingly hard to endure. ॥19॥
9.20: And she filled the quarters with the sound of her own bell, which brought about the destruction of the vigour of all the daitya armies. ॥20॥
9.21: Then the lion, with great roars that made elephants give up their great rut, filled the sky, the earth, and likewise the ten directions. ॥21॥
9.22: Then Kālī, leaping up into the sky, struck the earth with both hands; by that resounding the earlier sounds were drowned out. ॥22॥
9.23: Śivadūtī let out an ominous, booming laughter; at those sounds the asuras trembled, and Śumbha went into supreme rage. ॥23॥
9.24: When Ambikā cried out, “Stand, stand, O wicked one!”, then “Victory!” was proclaimed by the gods stationed in the sky. ॥24॥
9.25: The spear which Śumbha, having come forward, hurled, exceedingly dreadful with its flames and coming on like a mass of fire, was repelled by the Devī with a great meteor-like firebrand. ॥25॥
9.26: The space within the three worlds was filled by Śumbha’s lion-like roar; but the dreadful sound like a thunderclap of the Devī overpowered it, O lord of the earth. ॥26॥
9.27: The Devī cut down the arrows shot by Śumbha, and Śumbha the arrows sent by her, with their own fierce arrows, in hundreds and then in thousands. ॥27॥
9.28: Then that Caṇḍikā, enraged, struck him with her trident; and he, struck then, fell senseless to the ground. ॥28॥
9.29: Then Niśumbha, regaining consciousness and taking up his bow, struck with arrows the Devī, Kālī and the lion likewise. ॥29॥
9.30: And again, the lord of the Danujas, the son of Diti, making for himself ten thousand arms, covered Caṇḍikā with discus-weapons. ॥30॥
9.31: Then the blessed Durgā, the destroyer of distress in hardship, the Devī, enraged, cut down those discuses and those arrows with her own arrows. ॥31॥
9.32: Then Niśumbha, surrounded by the Daitya army, seizing a mace, rushed swiftly at Caṇḍikā to kill her. ॥32॥
9.33: As he was rushing upon her, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his mace with her sharp-edged sword; and he took up a trident. ॥33॥
9.34: As Niśumbha, the tormentor of the immortals, came on with trident in hand, Caṇḍikā pierced him in the heart with her trident, hurled with force. ॥34॥
9.35: From the heart of him, pierced by the trident, came forth another being, of great strength and great valour, saying ‘Stop!’ ॥35॥
9.36: As he was coming out, the Devī, laughing aloud, then cut off his head with her sword; thereupon he fell to the ground. ॥36॥
9.37: Then the lion devoured those asuras whose necks it had crushed with its fierce fangs, and likewise Kālī and Śivadūtī devoured others. ॥37॥
9.38: Some great asuras, pierced through by Kaumārī’s spear, perished; others were driven off by water sanctified by Brahmāṇī’s mantras. ॥38॥
9.39: Likewise others, pierced by Māheśvarī’s trident, fell; some were pounded to dust on the ground by the blows of Vārāhī’s snout. ॥39॥
9.40: Dānavas were cut to pieces by Vaiṣṇavī’s discus, and likewise others by the thunderbolt released from the tip of Aindrī’s hand. ॥40॥
9.41: Some asuras perished, some fled the great battle, and the rest Kālī, Śivadūtī and the lion, king of beasts, devoured. ॥41॥
9.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the ninth adhyāya, named the slaying of Niśumbha. ॥9॥
10.dhyana: Om. I worship in my heart Kāmeśvarī, radiant like molten gold, whose three eyes are the sun, the moon and fire, who holds in her lovely arms the bow and arrows together with the goad, the noose and the trident, who is the very form of Śiva and Śakti, and who wears the crescent moon.
10.2: Seeing his brother Niśumbha, dear to him as his own life, slain, and his army being slaughtered, Śumbha in anger spoke these words: ॥2॥
10.3: O Durgā, corrupted by the pride of strength, do not be arrogant! Relying on the strength of others, you fight, though you are so very haughty. ॥3॥
10.5: I alone exist here in the world; who else is there besides me? Behold, O wicked one, these, my own powers, entering into me alone! ॥5॥
10.6: Then all those goddesses, led by Brahmāṇī, went to dissolution in the body of that Devī; then Ambikā alone remained. ॥6॥
10.8: The many forms in which I stood here through my power have been withdrawn by me. I stand alone in battle; be steady! ॥8॥
10.10: Then began a terrible battle between the two, the Devī and Śumbha, while all the gods and demons looked on. ॥10॥
10.11: With showers of arrows, sharp weapons and most dreadful missiles, the battle between the two raged again, frightening all the worlds. ॥11॥
10.12: The hundreds of divine missiles that Ambikā then released, the lord of the Daityas broke with weapons that countered them. ॥12॥
10.13: And the divine missiles he released, the Supreme Devī broke as if in play, by fierce utterances of ‘huṃ’ and the like. ॥13॥
10.14: Then that Asura covered the Devī with hundreds of arrows; and the Devī, enraged at that, cut his bow with her arrows. ॥14॥
10.15: When his bow was cut, the lord of the Daityas then took up a spear; that too, as it rested in his hand, the Devī cut with her discus. ॥15॥
10.16: Then, seizing a sword and a shining shield bearing a hundred moons, the overlord of the Daityas rushed at that Devī. ॥16॥
10.17: Even as he rushed forward, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his sword, and his shield bright as the sun’s rays, with sharp arrows shot from her bow; and she struck down his horses and his chariot along with the charioteer. ॥17॥
10.18: Then that Daitya, his horses slain, his bow cut, without a charioteer, seized a dreadful mace, intent on killing Ambikā. ॥18॥
10.19: As he rushed on, she cut his mace with sharp arrows; even so he, swift, ran at her, raising his fist. ॥19॥
10.20: That bull among Daityas brought his fist down on the Devī’s heart; and the Devī too struck him on the chest with her palm. ॥20॥
10.21: Struck by the blow of her palm, that king of the Daityas fell to the ground, but at once rose up again just as before. ॥21॥
10.22: Leaping up and seizing the Devī, he rose high into the sky; there too Caṇḍikā, without any support, fought with him. ॥22॥
10.23: Then in the sky the Daitya and Caṇḍikā fought each other hand to hand, an unprecedented combat that filled the Siddhas and sages with wonder. ॥23॥
10.24: Then, having fought with him hand to hand for a long time, Ambikā lifted him up, whirled him around and hurled him to the ground. ॥24॥
10.25: Thrown down, he reached the earth, and, raising his fist, that swift and wicked-souled one rushed forward with the desire to kill Caṇḍikā. ॥25॥
10.26: Then, as he came on, the Devī pierced the lord of all the Daitya people in the chest with her spear and felled him to the ground. ॥26॥
10.27: Wounded by the point of the Devī’s spear, he fell lifeless to the ground, shaking the whole earth with its oceans, islands and mountains. ॥27॥
10.28: Then, when that evil-souled one was slain, the whole world became serene and attained great well-being, and the sky became clear. ॥28॥
10.29: The portentous clouds with meteors that had been there before subsided, and the rivers flowed within their courses when he was felled there. ॥29॥
10.30: Then, when he was slain, all the hosts of gods became joyful at heart, and the Gandharvas sang sweetly. ॥30॥
10.31: Likewise others played instruments, and the hosts of Apsarases danced; holy winds blew, and the sun shone brightly. ॥31॥
10.32: The sacred fires blazed up peacefully, and the ominous sounds arising from the quarters were stilled. ॥32॥
10.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the tenth adhyāya, named the slaying of Śumbha. ॥10॥
11.dhyana: Om. I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose radiance is like the rising sun, who wears the moon as her crown, who has high breasts and three eyes, whose face is smiling, and whose hands show the boon-giving gesture, the goad, the noose and the gesture of fearlessness.
11.2: When the great lord of the asuras had been slain there by the Devī, the gods together with Indra, led by Agni, praised her, Kātyāyanī, their lotus-faces blooming and the quarters brightened by them because they had gained their desire. ॥2॥
11.3: O Devī, who take away the suffering of those who come to you for refuge, be gracious! Be gracious, Mother of all the world! Be gracious, Mistress of the universe, and protect the universe! You, O Devī, rule over all that moves and is still. ॥3॥
11.4: You alone are the support of the world, since you abide in the form of the earth. By you, abiding in the form of water, all this is nourished, O you of inviolable valour. ॥4॥
11.5: You are the power of Viṣṇu, of infinite valour; you are the seed of the universe, the supreme Māyā. O Devī, all this world is deluded by you; you, when gracious, are the cause of liberation on earth. ॥5॥
11.6: All forms of knowledge, O Devī, are your aspects, and so are all women throughout the worlds. By you alone, the Mother, this world is pervaded. What praise can there be of you, who are yourself the higher and lower utterance of what is to be praised? ॥6॥
11.7: When you, the Devī who are all beings and the giver of enjoyment and liberation, have thus been praised, what excellent words could there be for further praise? ॥7॥
11.8: O Devī who dwell in the heart of every person in the form of intelligence, giver of heaven and final liberation, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥8॥
11.9: O you who, in the form of kalā, kāṣṭhā and other units of time, bring about transformation, O Power capable of the dissolution of the universe, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
11.10: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O Śivā, accomplisher of every aim, O refuge, O three-eyed Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥10॥
11.11: O eternal one, who are the power of creation, preservation and destruction, O abode of the guṇas, made of the guṇas, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥11॥
11.12: O you who are devoted to rescuing the wretched and afflicted who come to you for refuge, O Devī who remove the distress of all, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥12॥
11.13: O you who ride in the celestial car yoked with swans, bearing the form of Brahmāṇī, O Devī who sprinkle water with kuśa grass, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥13॥
11.14: O you who hold the trident, the moon and the serpent, who ride the great bull, in the form of Māheśvarī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥14॥
11.15: O sinless one, attended by peacocks and cocks, bearing the great spear, abiding in the form of Kaumārī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥15॥
11.16: O you who have taken up the supreme weapons—conch, discus, mace and the Śārṅga bow—be gracious, O you in the form of Vaiṣṇavī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥16॥
11.17: O you who hold the fierce great discus, who lifted up the earth on your tusk, O auspicious one in the form of the Boar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥17॥
11.18: O you who, in the fierce form of the Man-Lion, strove to slay the daityas, O you engaged in protecting the three worlds, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥18॥
11.19: O crowned one, wielder of the great thunderbolt, resplendent with a thousand eyes, O Aindrī, taker of Vṛtra’s life, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥19॥
11.20: O you who, in the form of Śivadūtī, slew the mighty host of the daityas, O you of terrible form and mighty roar, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥20॥
11.21: O you whose face is dreadful with fangs, adorned with a garland of heads, O Cāmuṇḍā, crusher of Muṇḍa, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥21॥
11.22: O Lakṣmī, O Modesty, O great Knowledge, O Faith, O Nourishment, O Svadhā, O Constant one, O great Night, O great Māyā, O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥22॥
11.23: O Medhā (intellect), O Sarasvatī, O excellent one, O Prosperity, O tawny Bābhravī, O dark Tāmasī, O Niyatā (self-restrained), O Sovereign, be gracious; O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you. ॥23॥
11.24: O you who are the form of all, Mistress of all, endowed with every power, protect us from fears, O Devī; O Devī Durgā, salutation to you. ॥24॥
11.25: May this gentle face of yours, adorned with three eyes, protect us from all beings. O Kātyāyanī, salutation be to you. ॥25॥
11.26: May your trident, fearsome with flames, exceedingly fierce, the destroyer of all the asuras, protect us from fear. O Bhadrakālī, salutation be to you. ॥26॥
11.27: O Devī, may that bell which, filling the world with its sound, destroys the might of the Daityas, protect us from sins, as a mother protects her children. ॥27॥
11.28: May your sword, smeared with the mire of the blood and fat of asuras and gleaming in your hand, be for our good. O Caṇḍikā, we bow to you. ॥28॥
11.29: When pleased, you destroy all diseases; but when angered, you destroy all desired wishes. For people who have taken refuge in you there is no calamity; those who have taken refuge in you indeed become a refuge for others. ॥29॥
11.30: This slaughter of the great asuras, haters of dharma, which you have wrought today, O Devī, having made your own form manifold through many forms — O Ambikā, what other goddess could accomplish that? ॥30॥
11.31: In the branches of knowledge, in the scriptures, and in the primeval utterances the Vedas that are lamps of discernment, who but you is spoken of? Who else makes this universe whirl about so intensely in the pit of attachment, filled with very great darkness? ॥31॥
11.32: Where there are rākṣasas, where there are serpents of fierce venom, where there are enemies, where there are hosts of robbers, where there is forest fire, and likewise in the midst of the ocean — there you stand and protect the universe. ॥32॥
11.33: O Queen of the universe, you protect the universe; as the soul of the universe you sustain the universe here. You are worthy of reverence by the lord of the universe; those who bow to you in devotion become the refuge of the universe. ॥33॥
11.34: O Devī, be gracious; protect us always from fear of enemies, just as you have done now, at once, by slaying the asuras. Quickly put an end to the sins of every world and to the great calamities born of the ripening of evil portents. ॥34॥
11.35: O Devī, remover of the world’s afflictions, be gracious to those who bow to you. O you who are worthy of praise by the dwellers of the three worlds, be the giver of boons to the worlds. ॥35॥
11.37: O hosts of gods, I am the giver of boons. Whatever boon you desire in your minds, choose it; I shall grant it, a boon beneficial to the worlds. ॥37॥
11.39: O Sovereign of all, may there be the quelling of all afflictions of the three worlds; and in just this way you must bring about the destruction of our enemies. ॥39॥
11.41: When the Vaivasvata Manvantara has come, in the twenty-eighth yuga, two other great asuras, Śumbha and Niśumbha, will be born. ॥41॥
11.42: Born in the house of the cowherd Nanda, arising from the womb of Yaśodā, I shall then destroy those two, dwelling on the Vindhya mountain. ॥42॥
11.43: Again, descending upon the earth in an exceedingly terrible form, I shall slay the Dānavas descended from Vipracitti. ॥43॥
11.44: And as I devour those fierce great asuras, the descendants of Vipracitti, my teeth will become red, like pomegranate flowers. ॥44॥
11.45: Then the gods in heaven and humans in the mortal world, praising me, will constantly call me Raktadantikā. ॥45॥
11.46: And again, when there is a drought lasting a hundred years without water, I, remembered by the sages, shall appear on earth, not born from a womb. ॥46॥
11.47: Then I shall look upon the sages with a hundred eyes; hence humans will celebrate me as ‘Śatākṣī’. ॥47॥
11.48: Then, O gods, until the rains come, I shall nourish the whole world with life-sustaining vegetables born from my own body. ॥48॥
11.49: Then I shall attain renown on earth as ‘Śākambharī’, and right there I shall slay the great asura named Durgama. ॥49॥
11.50: That name of mine, renowned as ‘Durgā Devī’, will come to be. And again, when, having assumed a terrible form on the Himālaya, ॥50॥
11.51: I shall devour the Rākṣasas for the sake of protecting the sages, then all the sages, with their bodies bowed low, will praise me. ॥51॥
11.52: That name of mine, renowned as ‘Bhīmā Devī’, will come to be. When the demon named Aruṇa causes great affliction in the three worlds, ॥52॥
11.53: then I, having assumed the form of bees, made up of countless bees, shall slay the great asura for the welfare of the three worlds. ॥53॥
11.54: And then people everywhere will praise me as ‘Bhrāmarī’. Thus, whenever affliction arising from the Dānavas occurs, ॥54॥
11.55: then, each time, I shall descend incarnate and bring about the destruction of the enemies. ॥55॥
11.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the eleventh adhyāya, named the praise of Nārāyaṇī. ॥11॥
12.dhyana: Om. I worship Durgā, the three-eyed, whose radiance equals the splendour of lightning, who is seated on the shoulder of the lion, who is fearsome, who is attended by maidens whose hands gleam with swords and shields, who holds in her hands the discus, mace, sword, shield, arrows, bow, bowstring and the threatening gesture (tarjanī), who is fiery in nature and bears the moon on her head.
12.2: Whoever, with a collected mind, constantly praises me with these hymns, all his affliction I will surely remove, without doubt. ॥2॥
12.3: Those who will recite the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the slaying of Mahiṣāsura, and likewise the killing of Śumbha and Niśumbha, ॥3॥
12.4: and those who, single-minded, will listen with devotion to my excellent Māhātmya on the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth lunar days, ॥4॥
12.5: to them no wrongdoing whatever, nor calamities arising from wrongdoing, will come; nor poverty, nor separation from loved ones. ॥5॥
12.6: For him there will never arise fear from enemies, from robbers, or from the king, nor from weapons, fire or floods of water. ॥6॥
12.7: Therefore this Māhātmya of mine should be recited by those of collected mind and always listened to with devotion; it is the supreme, great means of welfare. ॥7॥
12.8: My Māhātmya would pacify all calamities without remainder, including those arising from great epidemics, and likewise the threefold portent celestial, atmospheric and earthly. ॥8॥
12.9: The sanctuary of mine where this is properly recited every day, I will never abandon; my presence abides there. ॥9॥
12.10: At the offering of oblations, in worship, in fire rituals and at great festivals, this entire Māhātmya of mine should be recited and also caused to be heard. ॥10॥
12.11: Whether with knowledge or without knowledge, I will accept with love the offering and worship as performed, and likewise the fire oblation so performed. ॥11॥
12.12: At the great annual worship that is performed in the autumn season, one who, filled with devotion, hears this Māhātmya of mine, ॥12॥
12.13: a person, by my grace, will be freed from all afflictions and endowed with wealth and grain; there is no doubt. ॥13॥
12.14: Having heard this Māhātmya of mine, and likewise the accounts of my auspicious manifestations and my valour in battles, a man becomes fearless. ॥14॥
12.15: Enemies go to destruction, welfare is attained, and the family rejoices, of those men who listen to my Māhātmya. ॥15॥
12.16: In rites of pacification everywhere, likewise on seeing bad dreams, and in severe afflictions caused by the planets, one should listen to my Māhātmya. ॥16॥
12.17: Calamities subside, as do the dreadful planetary afflictions, and a bad dream seen by men turns into a good dream. ॥17॥
12.18: It brings peace to children seized by child-afflicting spirits, and it is the best means of creating friendship among men when their union is broken. ॥18॥
12.19: It supremely destroys the strength of all evildoers; by its mere recitation, rākṣasas, bhūtas and piśācas are destroyed. ॥19॥
12.20: This entire Māhātmya of mine brings about my presence. With animal offerings, flowers, arghya and incense, and likewise with excellent perfumes and lamps, ॥20॥
12.21: with the feeding of brāhmaṇas, with oblations, with consecrated sprinklings day and night, and with various other enjoyments and gifts over a year — the ॥21॥
12.22: pleasure that is produced in me, that same pleasure is produced when this is recited or heard even once. Heard, it takes away sins and likewise bestows health. ॥22॥
12.23: The recital of my manifestations gives protection from evil beings. My deeds in battles, the destruction of the wicked daityas — ॥23॥
12.24: when that is heard, fear caused by enemies does not arise for men. And the hymns which you gods have made, and those which the brahmarṣis have made, ॥24॥
12.25: And may those hymns composed by Brahmā grant you auspicious understanding. In a forest, or in a desolate wilderness, surrounded by a forest fire, ॥25॥
12.26: or surrounded by robbers in a lonely place, or seized by enemies, or pursued by lions and tigers, or in the forest by wild elephants, ॥26॥
12.27: or ordered by an angry king to be executed, or even placed in bonds, or tossed about by the wind while on a ship in the great ocean, ॥27॥
12.28: or while weapons are falling in a most terrible battle, or in all kinds of dreadful afflictions, or even tormented by pain — ॥28॥
12.29: a man who remembers this story of mine would be freed from distress. Through my power, lions and the like, robbers and likewise enemies ॥29॥
12.30: flee from afar from one who remembers my story. ॥30॥
12.32: Having spoken thus, that Blessed Caṇḍikā, of fierce valour, ॥32॥
12.33: vanished right there while all the gods looked on. And those gods too, free from fear, resumed their own offices as before, ॥33॥
12.34: all of them, partakers of shares in the sacrifice, their enemies slain, carried out their offices. And the daityas — when Śumbha, the enemy of the gods, had been slain in battle by the Devī, ॥34॥
12.35: when that destroyer of the world, extremely fierce and of incomparable valour, had been slain, and also Niśumbha of great might — those who remained went to Pātāla. ॥35॥
12.36: Thus that Blessed Devī, though eternal, manifesting again and again, O king, carries out the protection of the world. ॥36॥
12.37: By her this universe is deluded; she alone gives birth to the universe; and when entreated she grants knowledge, and when pleased, prosperity. ॥37॥
12.38: This entire cosmos, O lord of men, is pervaded by her — the Great Devī, Mahākālī, whose form is the Great Pestilence (Mahāmārī). ॥38॥
12.39: She herself, at the appointed time, is the Great Pestilence; she herself, the unborn, becomes creation; she herself, the eternal, sustains beings in due time. ॥39॥
12.40: In times of prosperity she herself is Lakṣmī in the homes of men, bestowing increase; and she herself, in times of want, becomes Alakṣmī for their ruin. ॥40॥
12.41: When praised and worshipped with flowers, incense, fragrances and the like, she gives wealth and sons, a mind set on dharma, and an auspicious destiny. ॥41॥
12.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the twelfth adhyāya, named the words of the Bhagavatī. ॥12॥
13.dhyana: Om. I worship Śivā, who shines like the orb of the rising sun, who has four arms and three eyes, and who holds the noose, the goad, and the gestures of boon-granting and fearlessness.
13.2: This excellent Glory of the Devī has been told to you, O king. Such is the power of that Devī by whom this world is upheld. ॥2॥
13.3: In the same way, knowledge is brought about by the divine Viṣṇumāyā. By her, you, this merchant, and likewise other discerning people— ॥3॥
13.4: —are being deluded, have been deluded, and others will fall into delusion. Go to her, O great king, the Supreme Sovereign Devī, for refuge. ॥4॥
13.5: When worshipped, she alone grants to human beings enjoyment, heaven and final liberation. ॥5॥
13.7: Having heard these words of his, Suratha, that lord of men, ॥7॥
13.8: having bowed down to that greatly blessed seer of rigorous vows, despondent through excessive attachment and through the seizure of his kingdom, ॥8॥
13.9: went at once to perform austerity, and so did the merchant, O great sage; for the sake of beholding Ambā, he settled on a river’s sandy bank. ॥9॥
13.10: And that merchant performed austerity, reciting the supreme Devī Sūkta. The two of them, having made an earthen image of the Devī on that river bank, ॥10॥
13.11: worshipped her with flowers, incense, fire offerings and libations, fasting, self-controlled, with minds fixed on her, and fully concentrated. ॥11॥
13.12: And the two offered a sacrifice sprinkled with blood from their own bodies. When, self-controlled, they had thus worshipped for three years, ॥12॥
13.13: Caṇḍikā, the Upholder of the world, fully pleased, spoke to them in visible form. ॥13॥
13.15: Whatever is asked for by you, O king, and by you, O joy of your family, receive all that from me. Fully pleased, I give it to you. ॥15॥
13.17: Then the king chose a kingdom that would not perish in another birth, and, in this very life, his own kingdom, with the forces of his enemies destroyed by his might. ॥17॥
13.18: Then that merchant too, wise and with a mind turned away from the world, chose the knowledge that dissolves attachment expressed as ‘mine’ and ‘I’. ॥18॥
13.20: In a very few days, O king, you will obtain your own kingdom. ॥20॥
13.21: Having slain your enemies, your kingdom will be unshaken for you there. ॥21॥
13.22: And when you have died, obtaining birth again from the god Vivasvat, ॥22॥
13.23: you will be on earth the Manu named Sāvarṇika. ॥23॥
13.24: And, O best of merchants, the boon that has been desired by you from me— ॥24॥
13.25: That which you have asked for I grant you for your complete perfection: knowledge will be yours. ॥25॥
13.27: Having thus given to the two of them the boon each desired, the Devī… ॥27॥
13.28: …vanished at once, praised with devotion by the two of them. Thus, having obtained the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, ॥28॥
13.29: having obtained birth from Sūrya, will become the Manu named Sāvarṇi. ॥29॥
13.end: Thus, having obtained the boon from the Devī, Suratha, the foremost of kṣatriyas, having obtained birth from Sūrya, will become the Manu Sāvarṇi. klīṃ oṃ.
13.iti: Svasti. Thus, in the Devī Māhātmya of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, in the account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara, ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named the boons to Suratha and the merchant. ॥13॥
aparadha.1: Om. Having committed a hundred offences, if one then cries out ‘O Mother of the world!’, the state one attains is not attained even by the gods headed by Brahmā. ॥1॥
aparadha.2: I am full of offences, and I have come to you for refuge, O Mother of the world. Now I deserve your compassion; do as you wish. ॥2॥
aparadha.3: Whatever has been done deficiently or in excess, through ignorance, forgetfulness or confusion, may all that be forgiven, O Devī; be gracious, O Supreme Ruler. ॥3॥
aparadha.4: O Kāmeśvarī, Mother of the world, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, accept this worship with love; be gracious, O Supreme Ruler. ॥4॥
aparadha.5: The Devī consists of all forms; the whole world is pervaded by the Devī. Therefore I bow to you, the Supreme Ruler, whose form is the universe. ॥5॥
aparadha.6: Whatever syllable has dropped out, and whatever may be lacking a mātrā (vowel length), may all that become complete by your grace, O Great Ruler. ॥6॥
aparadha.7: O Mother of the world, whatever I have uttered here in this recitation lacking a visarga, a bindu or a syllable, may that become fully complete through your grace, and may the fulfilment of my resolve always come about. ॥7॥
aparadha.8: O Mother, whatever in this hymn of yours has now been recited lacking a mātrā, a bindu, the pair of dots (visarga), a word, a pair of words, a letter and so on; with devotion or without devotion, in proper order or not, under the force of haste, clearly or indistinctly; whatever has been read or left unread through delusion or ignorance — may all that be complete with all its parts, O Bhagavatī, giver of boons, by your grace. Be gracious. ॥8॥
aparadha.9: Be gracious, O Bhagavatī, O Mother; be gracious, O you who love your devotees. Grant me your grace, O Devī; O Durgā, O Devī, salutation to you. ॥9॥
devi-sukta.1: Om. I move with the Rudras and with the Vasus; I move with the Ādityas and also with the Viśvedevas. I uphold both Mitra and Varuṇa; I uphold Indra and Agni; I uphold both the Aśvins. ॥1॥
devi-sukta.2: I uphold the swelling Soma; I uphold Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan and Bhaga. I bestow wealth on the sacrificer who offers oblations, who zealously serves the gods, who presses the Soma. ॥2॥
devi-sukta.3: I am the sovereign queen, the gatherer of riches, the knowing one, the first among those worthy of worship. Me, thus constituted, the gods have set down in many places, me who abide in many states and cause myself to enter into many beings. ॥3॥
devi-sukta.4: Through me he eats food, he who sees, he who breathes, he who hears what is spoken. Not knowing me, they dwell dependent on me. Hear, O famed one: I tell you what is worthy of faith. ॥4॥
devi-sukta.5: I myself declare this, which is welcomed by gods and by men alike. Whom I desire, him I make mighty; him I make a Brahmā, him a seer, him one of great wisdom. ॥5॥
devi-sukta.6: I string the bow for Rudra, so that his arrow may slay the hater of sacred speech. I make strife for the people against their foes; I have entered heaven and earth. ॥6॥
devi-sukta.7: I bring forth the father at the summit of this world; my origin is within the waters, in the ocean. From there I spread out over all the worlds, and I touch yonder heaven with my height. ॥7॥
devi-sukta.8: I alone blow forth like the wind, laying hold of all the worlds. Beyond heaven, beyond this earth — so vast have I become through my greatness. ॥8॥
devi-sukta.iti: Thus ends the Devī Sūkta, as the Ṛgveda gives it.
